216.body: Download the pre-built dictionary archive matching the CLI version from the GitHub releases page and install it under the OS-standard application data directory.
216.title: download

217.body: Dictionary name (required): one of ipadic, ipadic-neologd, unidic, sudachidict, ko-dic, cc-cedict, jieba --force: Re-download and replace an existing dictionary
217.title: Download parameters

218.body: Dictionaries are installed under a versioned layout <data dir>/dictionaries/<version>/lindera-<name>/. The default base directory per OS: OS Default location Linux ~/.local/share/lindera macOS ~/Library/Application Support/lindera Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%\lindera Set the LINDERA_DATA_DIR environment variable to override the base directory. This variable is unrelated to the build-time source cache variable LINDERA_BUILD_DICTIONARY_CACHE_DIR.
218.title: Storage location

219.body:
% lindera download ipadic Downloading https://github.com/lindera/lindera/releases/download/v5.1.0/lindera-ipadic-5.1.0.zip
100% (15.1/15.1 MiB)
Downloaded dictionary 'ipadic'
/home/user/.local/share/lindera/dictionaries/5.1.0/lindera-ipadic The installed path is printed to stdout (progress and notices go to stderr), so it can be captured in scripts: % DICT_DIR=$(lindera download ipadic) After downloading, the dictionary can be referenced by name in tokenize: % echo "日本語の形態素解析を行うことができます。" | lindera tokenize --dict ipadic Notes: The archive version always matches the CLI version; running a development build whose version has no published release yet fails with HTTP 404. Integrity is verified via the HTTPS transport and the ZIP archive's built-in per-file CRC32 checksums. The largest dictionary (ipadic-neologd) is a ~305 MB download and requires roughly twice that amount of free disk space during extraction.
219.title: Download usage

22.body: The LINDERA_WORKDIR environment variable is automatically set during the build process by the lindera-dictionary crate. It points to the directory containing the built dictionary data files and is used internally by dictionary crates to locate their data files. This variable is set automatically and should not be modified by users.
22.title: LINDERA_WORKDIR

220.body: Train a new morphological analysis model from annotated corpus data. To use this feature, you must build with the train feature flag enabled. (The train feature flag is enabled by default.)
220.title: train

221.body: --seed / -s: Seed lexicon file (CSV format) to be weighted --corpus / -c: Training corpus (annotated text) --char-def / -C: Character definition file (char.def) --unk-def / -u: Unknown word definition file (unk.def) to be weighted --feature-def / -f: Feature definition file (feature.def) --rewrite-def / -r: Rewrite rule definition file (rewrite.def) --output / -o: Output model file --lambda / -l: Regularization coefficient, finite and >= 0 (0 disables regularization); with l2, MeCab's learner's -c C is 1 / C (default: 1.0, MeCab's -c 1.0) --regularization / -R: Regularization type: l1, l2, or elasticnet, in any case; elastic_net and elastic-net also select Elastic Net (default: l2) --elastic-net-l1-ratio: L1 ratio for Elastic Net regularization (0.0-1.0), only used with --regularization elasticnet; 0 uses only L2, 1 uses only L1 (default: 0.5) --max-iterations / -i: Maximum number of iterations for training, 1 or more (default: 100) --eta / -e: Tolerance of the convergence test: training stops before --max-iterations once the relative change of the objective stays below this value for 3 iterations in a row; 0 disables the test (default: 0.00005, the default of MeCab's learner) --max-threads / -t: Maximum number of threads, 1 or more (defaults to CPU core count; affects only speed, never the trained model)
221.title: Train parameters

222.body:
1. Prepare training files Seed lexicon file (seed.csv): The seed lexicon file contains initial dictionary entries used for training the CRF model. Each line represents a word entry with comma-separated fields: Surface Left context ID Right context ID Word cost Part-of-speech tags (multiple fields) Base form Reading (katakana) Pronunciation Note: The exact field definitions differ between dictionary formats (IPADIC, UniDic, ko-dic, CC-CEDICT). Please refer to each dictionary's format specification for details. 外国,0,0,0,名詞,一般,*,*,*,*,外国,ガイコク,ガイコク
人,0,0,0,名詞,接尾,一般,*,*,*,人,ジン,ジン The file is read as CSV, as lindera build reads lex.csv: a field may be quoted (",",0,0,0,...), and a line that starts with # is an entry, not a comment. See Seed Lexicon for the details. Training corpus (corpus.txt): The training corpus file contains annotated text data used to train the CRF model. Each line consists of: A surface form (word) followed by a tab character Comma-separated morphological features (part-of-speech tags, base form, reading, pronunciation) Sentences are separated by "EOS" (End Of Sentence) markers 外国	名詞,一般,*,*,*,*,外国,ガイコク,ガイコク
人	名詞,接尾,一般,*,*,*,人,ジン,ジン
参政	名詞,サ変接続,*,*,*,*,参政,サンセイ,サンセイ
権	名詞,接尾,一般,*,*,*,権,ケン,ケン
EOS For detailed information about file formats and advanced features, see Training Pipeline . 2. Train model lindera train \ --seed ./resources/training/seed.csv \ --corpus ./resources/training/corpus.txt \ --unk-def ./resources/training/unk.def \ --char-def ./resources/training/char.def \ --feature-def ./resources/training/feature.def \ --rewrite-def ./resources/training/rewrite.def \ --output /tmp/lindera/training/model.dat \ --max-iterations 100 3. Training results lindera train writes the model to the --output file. Once it has built the training lattices, it prints how the gold tokens of the corpus were labelled (see How training works ). With the files in ./resources/training/: Lattice statistics: gold_lexicon=14 gold_unknown=0 gold_virtual=0 virtual_labels=0 negative_lexicon=0 negative_unknown=17 When no gold token is a seed word, or fewer than half of the gold tokens whose surface has seed rows are, it then writes a warning on stderr, with the first gold token whose surface has seed rows but none with its feature string, next to those rows (see How training works ). Once training stops, it prints why, with the number of iterations and of evaluations of the loss and its gradient (see --eta above): L-BFGS stopped after 8 iterations and 9 evaluations of the loss and its gradient: converged When an iteration left the objective unchanged or the line search failed far from the optimum, it then writes a warning on stderr (see How training works ). The trained model contains: Seed words : every seed lexicon row, with a learned weight and context IDs Unknown words : every unk.def entry, in file order, with a learned weight and context IDs Corpus words that are not in the seed lexicon are not added as words. They are learned through the unk.def entries, or through virtual labels, which are trained but not exported.
222.title: Basic workflow

223.body: Export a trained model file to Lindera dictionary format files. This feature requires building with the train feature flag enabled.
223.title: export

224.body: --model / -m: Path to the trained model file (.dat format) --output / -o: Directory to output the dictionary files --metadata: Optional metadata.json file to update with trained model information --cost-factor: Override cost factor for weight-to-cost conversion (default: value from trained model, typically 700)
224.title: Export parameters

225.body: The export command creates the following dictionary files in the output directory: lex.csv: Lexicon file with learned weights (MeCab-compatible cost via tocost()) matrix.def: Dense connection cost matrix covering all (right_id, left_id) pairs of the model's context IDs, plus 0 for BOS/EOS. A pair without a trained weight costs 0, as in training and in MeCab unk.def: Unknown word definitions, one line for each unk.def entry of the training input, in the same order char.def: Character type definitions feature.def: Feature template definitions (copied from trained model) rewrite.def: Feature rewrite rules (copied from trained model) left-id.def: Left context ID to feature string mapping right-id.def: Right context ID to feature string mapping metadata.json: Updated metadata file (if --metadata option is provided)
225.title: Output files

226.body: lindera export reads a model of the current format version (3.0.0) only. A model.dat written by an earlier version, which includes every model.dat written before 7.0.0, is rejected, and has to be trained again with lindera train. For a model trained with the 6.1.0 CLI: Error: LinderaError { kind: Deserialize, source: failed to deserialize model: failed without error information; enable debug assertions and the `alloc` feature in rancor for error information. The file is not a legacy JSON model either, so it was most likely written by a different version of lindera-trainer; re-run `lindera train` to regenerate it. }
226.breadcrumbs: Lindera CLI » Commands » Model format version
226.title: Model format version

227.body:
1. Train model lindera train \ --seed ./resources/training/seed.csv \ --corpus ./resources/training/corpus.txt \ --unk-def ./resources/training/unk.def \ --char-def ./resources/training/char.def \ --feature-def ./resources/training/feature.def \ --rewrite-def ./resources/training/rewrite.def \ --output /tmp/lindera/training/model.dat \ --max-iterations 100 2. Export to dictionary format lindera export \ --model /tmp/lindera/training/model.dat \ --metadata ./resources/training/metadata.json \ --output /tmp/lindera/training/dictionary 3. Build dictionary lindera build \ --src /tmp/lindera/training/dictionary \ --dest /tmp/lindera/training/compiled_dictionary \ --metadata /tmp/lindera/training/dictionary/metadata.json 4. Use trained dictionary echo "これは外国人参政権です。" | lindera tokenize -d /tmp/lindera/training/compiled_dictionary これ	名詞,代名詞,一般,*,*,*,これ,コレ,コレ
は	助詞,係助詞,*,*,*,*,は,ハ,ワ
外国	名詞,一般,*,*,*,*,外国,ガイコク,ガイコク
人	名詞,接尾,一般,*,*,*,人,ジン,ジン
参政	名詞,サ変接続,*,*,*,*,参政,サンセイ,サンセイ
権	名詞,接尾,一般,*,*,*,権,ケン,ケン
です	助動詞,*,*,*,特殊・デス,基本形,です,デス,デス
。	記号,句点,*,*,*,*,。,。,。
EOS
227.breadcrumbs: Lindera CLI » Commands » Complete workflow example
227.title: Complete workflow example

228.body: When the --metadata option is provided, the export command will: Read the base metadata.json file to preserve existing configuration Update specific fields with values from the trained model: default_word_cost: Calculated from feature weight median model_info: Training statistics including feature count, label count, matrix size (connection_matrix_size, the size of matrix.def as rows x columns), the number of training iterations that ran (training_iterations, at most --max-iterations), the regularization coefficient (regularization), its type (regularization_type: l1, l2 or elasticnet) and, for Elastic Net only, its L1 ratio (elastic_net_l1_ratio), and the model format version. No timestamp is written, so exporting the same model twice produces identical output Preserve existing settings such as dictionary name, character encoding, schema definitions, and other user-defined configuration

Use Unicode normalization and keep only common nouns: % echo "Ｌｉｎｄｅｒａは形態素解析ｴﾝｼﾞﾝです。" | lindera tokenize \ --dict ipadic \ --char-filter 'unicode_normalize:{"kind":"nfkc"}' \ --token-filter 'japanese_keep_tags:{"tags":["名詞,一般","名詞,サ変接続","名詞,固有名詞,組織"]}' Expected output: Lindera 名詞,固有名詞,組織,*,*,*,*,*,*

239.body: Lindera Python provides Python bindings for the Lindera morphological analysis engine, built with PyO3 . It brings Lindera's high-performance tokenization capabilities to the Python ecosystem with support for Python 3.10 and later.
239.title: Lindera Python

24.body: Lindera includes several example programs that demonstrate common use cases. The source code is available in the examples directory on GitHub (the tokenize* examples are in lindera-analysis/examples ). The tokenize* examples use the Tokenizer and filter APIs from lindera::analysis. They live in the lindera-analysis crate, hence -p lindera-analysis below. All examples below are run with the embed-ipadic feature enabled, which downloads the IPADIC dictionary and embeds it into the binary automatically at build time — no manual dictionary download is required.
24.title: Examples

240.body: Multi-language support : Tokenize Japanese (IPADIC, IPADIC NEologd, UniDic), Korean (ko-dic), and Chinese (CC-CEDICT, Jieba) text Text processing pipeline : Compose character filters and token filters for flexible preprocessing and postprocessing CRF-based dictionary training : Train custom morphological analysis models from annotated corpora (requires train feature) Multiple tokenization modes : Normal and decompose modes for different analysis granularity N-best tokenization : Retrieve multiple tokenization candidates ranked by cost User dictionaries : Extend system dictionaries with custom vocabulary
240.title: Features

250.body: This guide shows how to tokenize text using lindera-python.
250.breadcrumbs: Lindera Python » Quick Start » Quick Start

251.body:
The recommended way to create a tokenizer is through TokenizerBuilder: from lindera import Mode, TokenizerBuilder builder = TokenizerBuilder()
builder.set_mode(Mode.normal())
builder.set_dictionary("/path/to/ipadic")
tokenizer = builder.build() tokens = tokenizer.tokenize("関西国際空港限定トートバッグ")
for token in tokens: print(f"{token.surface}\t{','.join(token.details)}") Note: Download a pre-built dictionary from GitHub Releases and specify the path to the extracted directory. Expected output: 関西国際空港 名詞,固有名詞,組織,*,*,*,関西国際空港,カンサイコクサイクウコウ,カンサイコクサイクーコー
限定 名詞,サ変接続,*,*,*,*,限定,ゲンテイ,ゲンテイ
トートバッグ 名詞,一般,*,*,*,*,*,*,*

Each token exposes the following properties: from lindera import TokenizerBuilder tokenizer = TokenizerBuilder().set_dictionary("/path/to/ipadic").build()
tokens = tokenizer.tokenize("東京タワー") for token in tokens: print(f"Surface: {token.surface}") print(f"Byte range: {token.byte_start}..{token.byte_end}") print(f"Position: {token.position}") print(f"Word ID: {token.word_id}") print(f"Unknown: {token.is_unknown}") print(f"Details: {token.details}") print()

256.body: TokenizerBuilder configures and constructs a Tokenizer instance using the builder pattern.
256.title: TokenizerBuilder

257.body: TokenizerBuilder() Creates a new builder with default configuration. from lindera import TokenizerBuilder builder = TokenizerBuilder() TokenizerBuilder().from_file(file_path) Loads configuration from a YAML file and returns a new builder. See lindera-python/resources/lindera.yml for a complete example covering segmenter, character_filters, and token_filters. builder = TokenizerBuilder().from_file("lindera.yml")
257.title: Constructors

258.body:
All setter methods return self for method chaining. set_mode(mode) Sets the tokenization mode. mode is a Mode : Mode.normal() -- Standard tokenization (default) Mode.decompose(penalty=None) -- Decomposes compound words into smaller units, with the length penalties of a Penalty ; None uses the default penalty A value that is not a Mode, such as the string "normal", raises TypeError. To set a mode from its name, such as a configuration value, create it with Mode.from_str() . from lindera import Mode, Penalty builder.set_mode(Mode.normal())
builder.set_mode(Mode.decompose(Penalty(kanji_penalty_length_penalty=0)))
builder.set_mode(Mode.from_str("decompose")) set_dictionary(path) Sets the system dictionary path or URI. # Use an embedded dictionary
builder.set_dictionary("embedded://ipadic") # Use an external dictionary
builder.set_dictionary("/path/to/dictionary") set_user_dictionary(uri) Sets the user dictionary URI. builder.set_user_dictionary("/path/to/user_dictionary.csv") set_keep_whitespace(keep) Controls whether whitespace tokens appear in the output. Kept whitespace also stays in the lattice, so the other tokens can differ from those of the default output, which skips whitespace in the lattice as MeCab does. To keep whitespace in the lattice without outputting it, use set_skip_whitespace(False) instead. builder.set_keep_whitespace(True) set_skip_whitespace(skip) Sets whether whitespace is skipped in the lattice. skip has the same meaning as segmenter.skip_whitespace in a configuration file : True -- Skips whitespace, so the words on either side of it connect directly, as MeCab does. False -- Keeps whitespace in the lattice as a node of its own (a whitespace dictionary entry or the SPACE unknown word), as before v7. Whitespace is still dropped from the output. None -- The default of the dictionary's metadata.json: skipping, except with SudachiDict. Use it to undo an earlier call. A value set here overrides the dictionary's default and a skip_whitespace loaded with from_file. It has no effect while whitespace tokens are kept (set_keep_whitespace(True)), because kept whitespace always stays in the lattice. Any other value raises TypeError. With IPADIC, for example, Google が 新しい reads が as a particle (助詞) by default and as a conjunction (接続詞) with set_skip_whitespace(False). See Segmenter for details. # Keep whitespace in the lattice, as before v7
builder.set_skip_whitespace(False) set_space_penalty(value) Sets the left-space penalty for Korean: a candidate that starts right after whitespace and whose part-of-speech tag normally attaches to the preceding word (particles, endings, ...) gets a cost added. value has the same meaning as segmenter.space_penalty in a configuration file : None -- The default: the rules the dictionary ships in its metadata.json, if any (ko-dic ships mecab-ko-dic's rules; the other bundled dictionaries ship none). Use it to undo an earlier call. False -- Turns the penalty off. True -- Requires the dictionary's rules; build() raises ValueError for a dictionary that ships none. A dict of the form {"rules": [{"pos": [...], "cost": n}, ...]} -- Applies these rules instead. A candidate whose first part-of-speech tag is listed in pos gets cost added; the first matching rule wins. Any other value raises ValueError (a value with no JSON equivalent, such as an arbitrary object, raises TypeError, as in append_token_filter). # Turn the penalty off
builder.set_space_penalty(False) # Explicit rules
builder.set_space_penalty({ "rules": [ {"pos": ["EC", "EF", "EP", "ETM", "ETN", "VCP", "XSA", "XSN", "XSV"], "cost": 3000}, {"pos": ["JC", "JKB", "JKC", "JKG", "JKO", "JKQ", "JKS", "JKV", "JX"], "cost": 6000}, ]
}) [!NOTE] Since v6.1.0, ko-dic applies the left-space penalty by default, as mecab-ko does. For example, 검색 이 잘 된다 reads 이 as the interjection IC; without the penalty, as the subject particle JKS. Call builder.set_space_penalty(False) to turn it off. Only a ko-dic built by Lindera 6.1.0 or later ships the rules; with a ko-dic from the v6.0.0 release the penalty stays off and True fails until the dictionary is rebuilt. See Segmenter for details. append_character_filter(kind, args=None) Appends a character filter to the preprocessing pipeline. builder.append_character_filter("unicode_normalize", {"kind": "nfkc"}) append_token_filter(kind, args=None) Appends a token filter to the postprocessing pipeline. builder.append_token_filter("lowercase", {}) The arguments of set_space_penalty, append_character_filter and append_token_filter may nest lists and dicts at most 128 levels deep. A deeper value, or one that contains itself, raises ValueError.

258.title: Configuration Methods

26.title: segment

260.body: Tokenizer performs morphological analysis on text.
260.title: Tokenizer

261.body:
Tokenizer(dictionary, mode=None, user_dictionary=None, space_penalty=None) Creates a tokenizer directly from a loaded dictionary. mode takes a Mode , as TokenizerBuilder.set_mode does; None (the default) is normal mode. Any other value, such as the string "normal", raises TypeError. space_penalty takes the same values as TokenizerBuilder.set_space_penalty . None (the default) uses the left-space penalty rules the dictionary ships, so with ko-dic the penalty is on; pass False to turn it off. An invalid setting raises the same errors as set_space_penalty and build(). from lindera import Mode, Tokenizer, load_dictionary dictionary = load_dictionary("embedded://ipadic")
tokenizer = Tokenizer(dictionary, mode=Mode.normal()) # ko-dic without the left-space penalty
ko_tokenizer = Tokenizer(load_dictionary("embedded://ko-dic"), space_penalty=False)
261.breadcrumbs: Lindera Python » Tokenizer API » Creating a Tokenizer
261.title: Creating a Tokenizer

262.body:
tokenize(text) Tokenizes the input text and returns a list of Token objects. tokens = tokenizer.tokenize("形態素解析") Parameters: Name Type Description text str Text to tokenize Returns: list[Token] tokenize_surfaces(text) Tokenizes the input text and returns only the token surfaces, as a list of strings. This is the fast path for wakati-style use: no Token objects are created and no morphological details are loaded, so it is significantly faster than tokenize when only the surface strings are needed. The result equals [t.surface for t in tokenizer.tokenize(text)]. surfaces = tokenizer.tokenize_surfaces("形態素解析")
# ["形態素", "解析"] Parameters: Name Type Description text str Text to tokenize Returns: list[str] tokenize_nbest(text, n, unique=False, cost_threshold=None) Returns the N-best tokenization results, each paired with its total path cost. results = tokenizer.tokenize_nbest("すもももももももものうち", n=3)
for tokens, cost in results: print(cost, [t.surface for t in tokens]) Parameters: Name Type Description text str Text to tokenize n int Number of results to return unique bool Deduplicate results (default: False) cost_threshold int or None Maximum cost difference from the best path (default: None) Returns: list[tuple[list[Token], int]]
262.breadcrumbs: Lindera Python » Tokenizer API » Tokenizer Methods
262.title: Tokenizer Methods

263.body: Mode is the tokenization mode that TokenizerBuilder.set_mode() and the Tokenizer constructor take. It is the counterpart of the Rust lindera::mode::Mode: normal mode, or decompose mode with its Penalty .
263.title: Mode

264.body:
Mode has no constructor, so Mode() raises TypeError, and it has no Mode.Normal or Mode.Decompose attributes. Create a mode with one of the following static methods. Mode.normal() Returns normal mode: standard tokenization. Mode.decompose(penalty=None) Returns decompose mode, which adds the length penalties of penalty to the cost of long words, so that compound words are decomposed into smaller units. None (the default) uses the default penalty, Penalty(). A value that is not a Penalty raises TypeError. Mode.from_str(name) Returns the mode named name, as the Rust Mode parses a name: "normal" for normal mode, and "decompose" for decompose mode with the default penalty. Use it for a mode name read at run time, such as a configuration value. The name is case sensitive: any other name, such as "Normal", raises ValueError with the message Invalid mode. A value that is not a str raises TypeError. from lindera import Mode, Penalty normal = Mode.normal()
decompose = Mode.decompose()
whole_words = Mode.decompose(Penalty(kanji_penalty_length_penalty=0, other_penalty_length_penalty=0))
from_name = Mode.from_str("decompose") # equal to Mode.decompose()
264.breadcrumbs: Lindera Python » Tokenizer API » Creating a Mode
264.title: Creating a Mode

265.body: Both properties are read-only: Property Type Description name str "normal" or "decompose" penalty Penalty or None A copy of the penalty of decompose mode; None for normal mode
265.breadcrumbs: Lindera Python » Tokenizer API » Mode Properties
265.title: Mode Properties

266.body:
Method Returns Description __str__() str The name: "normal" or "decompose" __repr__() str "Mode.normal()", or Mode.decompose(...) with the penalty __eq__(other) bool True if other is a Mode with the same name and penalty is_normal() bool True for normal mode is_decompose() bool True for decompose mode mode = Mode.decompose()
mode.name # 'decompose'
mode.penalty # Penalty(kanji_threshold=2, kanji_penalty=3000, other_threshold=7, other_penalty=1700)
str(mode) # 'decompose'
repr(mode) # 'Mode.decompose(Penalty(kanji_threshold=2, kanji_penalty=3000, other_threshold=7, other_penalty=1700))'
mode.is_normal() # False
mode.is_decompose() # True
Mode.normal().penalty # None
repr(Mode.normal()) # 'Mode.normal()' Two modes are equal when their names and penalties are, as the Rust Mode compares them. A Mode is never equal to a value of another type, such as the string "normal": Mode.from_str("decompose") == Mode.decompose() # True
Mode.decompose() == Mode.decompose(Penalty(kanji_penalty_length_penalty=0)) # False
Mode.normal() == "normal" # False A Mode cannot be changed. Setting a property raises AttributeError, and penalty returns a copy, so changing the returned Penalty leaves the mode as it was; Mode.decompose() keeps a copy of the Penalty it is given as well. A Mode is not hashable, as the Rust Mode implements Eq but not Hash: hash(mode) raises TypeError, so a Mode cannot be a dict key or a set member. mode = Mode.decompose()
penalty = mode.penalty
penalty.kanji_penalty_length_penalty = 0
mode.penalty.kanji_penalty_length_penalty # 3000
266.title: Methods

267.body: Penalty configures the length-based penalty thresholds used by decompose mode segmentation.
267.title: Penalty

268.body:
Penalty(kanji_penalty_length_threshold=2, kanji_penalty_length_penalty=3000, other_penalty_length_threshold=7, other_penalty_length_penalty=1700) All arguments are optional and default to the values shown above. from lindera import Penalty penalty = Penalty( kanji_penalty_length_threshold=2, kanji_penalty_length_penalty=3000, other_penalty_length_threshold=7, other_penalty_length_penalty=1700,
)
268.breadcrumbs: Lindera Python » Tokenizer API » Creating a Penalty
268.title: Creating a Penalty

269.body:
All four fields support both getting and setting: Property Type Default Description kanji_penalty_length_threshold int 2 Kanji-only surface length above which the penalty applies kanji_penalty_length_penalty int 3000 Cost penalty added for kanji-only surfaces longer than the threshold other_penalty_length_threshold int 7 Surface length above which the penalty applies for non-kanji-only surfaces other_penalty_length_penalty int 1700 Cost penalty added for non-kanji-only surfaces longer than the threshold penalty.kanji_penalty_length_threshold = 3
print(penalty.kanji_penalty_length_threshold) # 3
269.breadcrumbs: Lindera Python » Tokenizer API » Penalty Properties

27.body: Basic tokenization using an external IPADIC dictionary. Segments input text and prints each token with its part-of-speech details. cargo run -p lindera-analysis --features=embed-ipadic --example=tokenize
27.title: tokenize

270.body:
Pass a Penalty to Mode.decompose() , and the mode to TokenizerBuilder.set_mode() or to the Tokenizer constructor . Without length penalties, decompose mode keeps long words whole: from lindera import Mode, Penalty, Tokenizer, TokenizerBuilder, load_dictionary text = "関西国際空港限定トートバッグ"
penalty = Penalty(kanji_penalty_length_penalty=0, other_penalty_length_penalty=0) builder = TokenizerBuilder().set_dictionary("embedded://ipadic")
tokenizer = builder.set_mode(Mode.decompose()).build()
print([token.surface for token in tokenizer.tokenize(text)])
# ['関西', '国際', '空港', '限定', 'トートバッグ'] tokenizer = builder.set_mode(Mode.decompose(penalty)).build()
print([token.surface for token in tokenizer.tokenize(text)])
# ['関西国際空港', '限定', 'トートバッグ'] tokenizer = Tokenizer(load_dictionary("embedded://ipadic"), mode=Mode.decompose(penalty))
print([token.surface for token in tokenizer.tokenize(text)])
# ['関西国際空港', '限定', 'トートバッグ'] Normal mode has no penalty: Mode.normal() takes no arguments.
270.breadcrumbs: Lindera Python » Tokenizer API » Using a Penalty
270.title: Using a Penalty

271.body: Token represents a single morphological token.
271.title: Token

272.body: Property Type Description surface str Surface form of the token byte_start int Start byte position in the original text byte_end int End byte position in the original text position int Token position index word_id int Dictionary word ID is_unknown bool True if the word is not in the dictionary details list[str] or None Morphological details (part of speech, reading, etc.)
272.title: Properties

273.body:
get_detail(index) Returns the detail string at the specified index, or None if the index is out of range. token = tokenizer.tokenize("東京")[0]
pos = token.get_detail(0) # e.g., "名詞"
subpos = token.get_detail(1) # e.g., "固有名詞"
reading = token.get_detail(7) # e.g., "トウキョウ" Parameters: Name Type Description index int Zero-based index into the details list Returns: str or None to_dict() Returns the token as a plain dict, keeping each field's natural Python type, so it serializes without a custom encoder. import json data = tokenizer.tokenize("東京")[0].to_dict()
# {'surface': '東京', 'byte_start': 0, 'byte_end': 6, 'position': 0,
# 'word_id': 12345, 'is_unknown': False, 'details': [...]} json.dumps([token.to_dict() for token in tokens]) Returns: dict with the keys surface, byte_start, byte_end, position, word_id, is_unknown, and details. The structure of details depends on the dictionary: IPADIC : [品詞, 品詞細分類1, 品詞細分類2, 品詞細分類3, 活用型, 活用形, 原形, 読み, 発音] UniDic : Detailed morphological features following the UniDic specification ko-dic / CC-CEDICT / Jieba : Dictionary-specific detail formats
273.breadcrumbs: Lindera Python » Tokenizer API » Token Methods
273.title: Token Methods

274.body:
Lindera Python functions raise standard Python exceptions rather than a custom exception type: IOError (an alias of OSError) -- for I/O-related failures, such as a missing or unreadable file ValueError -- for everything else, such as invalid configuration, parse errors, or tokenization failures from lindera import load_dictionary try: dictionary = load_dictionary("/path/that/does/not/exist")
except ValueError as e: print(f"Failed to load dictionary: {e}") A LinderaError class is also registered as lindera.LinderaError, but no function in this crate currently raises it -- it can only be constructed and raised manually. Catch IOError/ValueError (or the general Exception) when handling errors from this library, not LinderaError.
274.breadcrumbs: Lindera Python » Tokenizer API » Error Handling
274.title: Error Handling

275.body: Lindera Python provides functions for loading, building, and managing dictionaries used in morphological analysis.
275.breadcrumbs: Lindera Python » Dictionary Management » Dictionary Management
275.title: Dictionary Management

276.breadcrumbs: Lindera Python » Dictionary Management » Loading Dictionaries
276.title: Loading Dictionaries

277.body:
Use load_dictionary(uri) to load a system dictionary. Download a pre-built dictionary from GitHub Releases and specify the path to the extracted directory: from lindera import load_dictionary dictionary = load_dictionary("/path/to/ipadic") Embedded dictionaries (advanced) -- if you built with an embed-* feature flag, you can load an embedded dictionary: dictionary = load_dictionary("embedded://ipadic") A loaded Dictionary also exposes its own metadata: print(dictionary.metadata_name()) # e.g. "ipadic"
print(dictionary.metadata_encoding()) # e.g. "UTF-8"
metadata = dictionary.metadata() # the full Metadata object A user dictionary must share the metadata (schema, encoding, etc.) of the system dictionary it augments. load_user_dictionary_for takes the system dictionary and uses its metadata, as in lindera-python/examples/tokenize_with_userdict.py (see User Dictionaries ).
277.breadcrumbs: Lindera Python » Dictionary Management » System Dictionaries
277.title: System Dictionaries

278.body:
User dictionaries add custom vocabulary on top of a system dictionary. Load one for the system dictionary it is used with: from lindera import load_dictionary, load_user_dictionary_for dictionary = load_dictionary("/path/to/ipadic")
user_dict = load_user_dictionary_for("/path/to/user_dictionary.csv", dictionary) A .csv is built with the system dictionary's metadata and checked against its connection matrix as it is built: a row whose context ID lies outside the matrix raises a ValueError that names its CSV line and surface (see Context IDs ). A .bin is loaded as it was built. load_user_dictionary(uri, metadata) loads a user dictionary with metadata only. A .csv loaded this way is checked when it is combined with the system dictionary, and the error names the entry by its word id: from lindera import load_user_dictionary, Metadata metadata = Metadata()
user_dict = load_user_dictionary("/path/to/user_dictionary.csv", metadata) Pass the user dictionary when building a tokenizer: from lindera import Mode, Tokenizer, load_dictionary, load_user_dictionary_for dictionary = load_dictionary("/path/to/ipadic")
user_dict = load_user_dictionary_for("/path/to/user_dictionary.csv", dictionary) tokenizer = Tokenizer(dictionary, mode=Mode.normal(), user_dictionary=user_dict) Or via the builder: from lindera import TokenizerBuilder tokenizer = ( TokenizerBuilder() .set_dictionary("/path/to/ipadic") .set_user_dictionary("/path/to/user_dictionary.csv") .build()
)
278.breadcrumbs: Lindera Python » Dictionary Management » User Dictionaries
278.title: User Dictionaries

279.breadcrumbs: Lindera Python » Dictionary Management » Building Dictionaries
279.title: Building Dictionaries

28.body: Tokenization with a user dictionary. Shows how to supplement the dictionary with custom entries for domain-specific terms. cargo run -p lindera-analysis --features=embed-ipadic --example=tokenize_with_user_dict
28.title: tokenize_with_user_dict

280.body:
Build a system dictionary from source files: from lindera import build_dictionary, Metadata metadata = Metadata(name="custom", encoding="UTF-8")
build_dictionary("/path/to/input_dir", "/path/to/output_dir", metadata) The input directory should contain the dictionary source files (CSV lexicon, matrix.def, etc.). Metadata loaded with Metadata.from_json_file keeps the space_penalty rules of the metadata.json, and the built dictionary ships them. For ko-dic this means the left-space penalty stays on by default in the dictionary you build; turn it off per tokenizer with TokenizerBuilder.set_space_penalty(False) (see Tokenizer API ). A Metadata created with the constructor carries no rules.
280.breadcrumbs: Lindera Python » Dictionary Management » System Dictionary
280.title: System Dictionary

281.body:
Build a user dictionary from a CSV file for the system dictionary it is used with: from lindera import build_user_dictionary_for, load_dictionary, load_user_dictionary_for dictionary = load_dictionary("/path/to/ipadic")
build_user_dictionary_for("user_words.csv", "/path/to/user_dictionary.bin", dictionary)
user_dict = load_user_dictionary_for("/path/to/user_dictionary.bin", dictionary) The CSV is built with the system dictionary's metadata and checked against its connection matrix: a row whose context ID lies outside the matrix raises a ValueError that names its CSV line and surface, and no file is written (see Context IDs ). The second argument is the path of the file to write. End it with .bin, since the loaders choose how to load a user dictionary by its extension. build_user_dictionary(kind, input_file, output_dir, metadata) builds a user dictionary with metadata only. Despite its name, output_dir is the path of the file to write too, not a directory. The rows are checked when the user dictionary is combined with the system dictionary, and the error names the entry by its word id: from lindera import build_user_dictionary, Metadata metadata = Metadata()
build_user_dictionary("ipadic", "user_words.csv", "/path/to/user_dictionary.bin", metadata) The metadata parameter is optional. When omitted, default metadata values are used: build_user_dictionary("ipadic", "user_words.csv", "/path/to/user_dictionary.bin") Note: the first argument ("ipadic" above) is currently unused and reserved for future use -- it does not select or configure the build in any way. Removes tokens whose part-of-speech matches any of the specified tags. tokenizer = ( TokenizerBuilder() .set_dictionary("embedded://ipadic") .append_token_filter("japanese_stop_tags", { "tags": ["助詞,格助詞,一般", "助詞,係助詞", "助詞,連体化", "助動詞"], }) .build()
) Tags are normalized to exactly four comma-separated levels (missing levels are padded with *) and compared for exact equality against the four part-of-speech details of each token, starting at the field named part_of_speech in the dictionary schema (or at the first detail when the schema has no such field). A bare 助詞 therefore never matches IPADIC particle tokens — they always carry a subcategory such as 助詞,係助詞 — while a bare 助動詞 does match, because auxiliary verbs have no subcategory (助動詞,*,*,*).

303.body: Lindera Python supports training custom CRF-based morphological analysis models from annotated corpora. This functionality requires the train feature.
303.title: Training

304.body: Build lindera-python with the train feature enabled (enabled by default): maturin develop --features train

305.body:
Use lindera.train() to train a CRF model from a seed lexicon and annotated corpus: import lindera lindera.train( seed="resources/training/seed.csv", corpus="resources/training/corpus.txt", char_def="resources/training/char.def", unk_def="resources/training/unk.def", feature_def="resources/training/feature.def", rewrite_def="resources/training/rewrite.def", output="/tmp/model.dat", lambda_=1.0, max_iter=100, max_threads=4,
)

306.body: Parameter Type Default Description seed str required Path to the seed lexicon file (CSV format) corpus str required Path to the annotated training corpus char_def str required Path to the character definition file (char.def) unk_def str required Path to the unknown word definition file (unk.def) feature_def str required Path to the feature definition file (feature.def) rewrite_def str required Path to the rewrite rule definition file (rewrite.def) output str required Output path for the trained model file lambda_ float 1.0 Regularization coefficient, finite and >= 0; 0 disables regularization for every type; with L2, MeCab's -c C is 1 / C, so 1.0 is MeCab's -c 1.0 max_iter int 100 Maximum number of training iterations, 1 or more; training stops earlier once the objective converges (see eta) max_threads int or None None Number of threads, 1 or more (None = auto-detect CPU cores) regularization str "l2" Regularization type: "l1", "l2" or "elasticnet", in any case ("elastic_net" and "elastic-net" also select Elastic Net), as lindera train --regularization takes it elastic_net_l1_ratio float 0.5 L1 ratio of Elastic Net regularization, between 0 and 1; 0 uses only L2, 1 uses only L1; used only with "elasticnet" eta float 5e-5 Tolerance of the convergence test, finite and >= 0: training stops before max_iter once the relative change of the objective stays below it for 3 iterations in a row; 0 disables the test The settings are checked before any file is read: an unknown regularization, or a lambda_, elastic_net_l1_ratio or eta outside its range, raises a ValueError. To train with v6's default settings (the model still differs from v6's, since the first line search changed in #1290 ), pass regularization="l1" and lambda_=0.01, and eta=0 to stop only at max_iter.
306.title: Training Parameters

307.body:
After training, export the model to dictionary source files using lindera.export(): import lindera lindera.export( model="/tmp/model.dat", output="/tmp/dictionary_source", metadata="resources/training/metadata.json",
)

308.body: Parameter Type Default Description model str required Path to the trained model file (.dat) output str required Output directory for dictionary source files metadata str or None None Path to a base metadata.json file The export creates the following files in the output directory, the same files that lindera export creates: lex.csv -- Lexicon entries with trained costs matrix.def -- Connection cost matrix unk.def -- Unknown word definitions char.def -- Character category definitions (copied from the trained model) feature.def -- Feature template definitions (copied from the trained model) rewrite.def -- Feature rewrite rules (copied from the trained model) left-id.def -- Left context ID to feature string mapping right-id.def -- Right context ID to feature string mapping metadata.json -- Updated metadata (when metadata parameter is provided) The model file must come from this version's training. A model file written by an earlier version, which includes every model file written before 7.0.0, is rejected: lindera.export() fails with an error that asks you to re-run training. Train such a model again with lindera.train().

33.body: Morphological analysis is the process of breaking down text into its smallest meaningful units (morphemes) and identifying their grammatical properties. For languages like Japanese, Chinese, and Korean -- where words are not separated by spaces -- morphological analysis is an essential first step for natural language processing tasks such as search indexing, text classification, and machine translation.

330.body: TokenizerBuilder configures and constructs a Tokenizer instance using the builder pattern.
330.title: TokenizerBuilder

331.body: new TokenizerBuilder() Creates a new builder with default configuration. const { TokenizerBuilder } = require("lindera"); const builder = new TokenizerBuilder(); new TokenizerBuilder().fromFile(filePath) Loads configuration from a YAML file and returns a new builder. const builder = new TokenizerBuilder().fromFile("lindera.yml"); See lindera-nodejs/resources/lindera.yml for a complete example configuration file, including dictionary, character filter, and token filter settings.
331.title: Constructors

332.body:
All setter methods return the builder itself (this), so they can be chained or called one statement at a time. setMode(mode) Sets the tokenization mode, a Mode : Mode.normal() -- Standard tokenization (default) Mode.decompose(penalty?) -- Decomposes compound words into smaller units, with the Penalty the mode holds A value that is not a Mode, such as the mode name "normal", throws an InvalidArg error. A mode name read at run time, such as a setting, becomes a Mode with Mode.fromStr() . const { Mode } = require("lindera"); builder.setMode(Mode.normal());
builder.setMode(Mode.decompose({ kanjiPenaltyLengthPenalty: 0 }));
builder.setMode(Mode.fromStr("decompose")); setDictionary(path) Sets the system dictionary path or URI. // Use an embedded dictionary
builder.setDictionary("embedded://ipadic"); // Use an external dictionary
builder.setDictionary("/path/to/dictionary"); setUserDictionary(uri) Sets the user dictionary URI. builder.setUserDictionary("/path/to/user_dictionary.csv"); setKeepWhitespace(keep) Controls whether whitespace tokens appear in the output. Kept whitespace also stays in the lattice, so the other tokens can differ from those of the default output, which skips whitespace in the lattice as MeCab does. To keep whitespace in the lattice without outputting it, use setSkipWhitespace(false) instead. builder.setKeepWhitespace(true); setSkipWhitespace(skip) Sets whether whitespace is skipped in the lattice. The value means the same as segmenter.skip_whitespace in a configuration file . Value Effect true Skips whitespace, so the words on either side of it connect directly, as MeCab does false Keeps whitespace in the lattice as a node of its own (a whitespace dictionary entry or the SPACE unknown word), as before v7; whitespace is still dropped from the output null or undefined Default: the setting of the dictionary's metadata.json (skipping, except with SudachiDict) A value set here overrides the dictionary's default and a skip_whitespace loaded with fromFile. It has no effect while whitespace tokens are kept (setKeepWhitespace(true)), because kept whitespace always stays in the lattice. The argument is required; any other value throws an Error. With IPADIC, for example, Google が 新しい reads が as a particle (助詞) by default and as a conjunction (接続詞) with setSkipWhitespace(false). See Segmenter for details. // Keep whitespace in the lattice, as before v7
builder.setSkipWhitespace(false); // Back to the dictionary's default
builder.setSkipWhitespace(null); setSpacePenalty(value) Sets the left-space penalty for Korean (mecab-ko's left-space-penalty-factor): a candidate that starts right after whitespace and whose first part-of-speech tag is listed in a rule gets that rule's cost added. The value means the same as segmenter.space_penalty in a configuration file . Value Effect null or undefined Default: the rules the dictionary ships in its metadata.json, if any false Turns the penalty off true Requires the dictionary's rules; build() throws if the dictionary ships none { rules: [{ pos: [...], cost: n }, ...] } Applies these rules instead of the dictionary's Any other value throws an Error. // Turn the penalty off
builder.setSpacePenalty(false); // Explicit rules (these are the ones ko-dic ships)
builder.setSpacePenalty({ rules: [ { pos: ["EC", "EF", "EP", "ETM", "ETN", "VCP", "XSA", "XSN", "XSV"], cost: 3000 }, { pos: ["JC", "JKB", "JKC", "JKG", "JKO", "JKQ", "JKS", "JKV", "JX"], cost: 6000 }, ],
}); // Back to the dictionary's default
builder.setSpacePenalty(null); [!NOTE] Since v6.1.0, ko-dic applies the left-space penalty by default, because its metadata.json ships mecab-ko-dic's rules. This changes the Korean output (for example, 이 in 검색 이 잘 된다 is the interjection IC with the penalty and the subject particle JKS without it). Call setSpacePenalty(false) to turn it off. For a Tokenizer created directly, pass false as the fourth argument: new Tokenizer(dictionary, Mode.normal(), null, false). A ko-dic downloaded from the v6.0.0 release ships no rules, so with it the penalty stays off and setSpacePenalty(true) makes build() throw. See Segmenter for details. appendCharacterFilter(kind, args?) Appends a character filter to the preprocessing pipeline. builder.appendCharacterFilter("unicode_normalize", { kind: "nfkc" }); appendTokenFilter(kind, args?) Appends a token filter to the postprocessing pipeline. builder.appendTokenFilter("lowercase", {}); The arguments of setSpacePenalty, appendCharacterFilter and appendTokenFilter may nest arrays and objects at most 128 levels deep. A deeper value, or one that contains itself, throws an Error.

34.body: Lindera is a dictionary-based morphological analyzer. It uses a pre-compiled system dictionary containing known words along with their costs, and applies the Viterbi algorithm to find the optimal segmentation of input text. The analysis process works as follows: Sentence splitting : Before building the lattice, Lindera splits the input text into sentences at delimiter characters (\n, \t, 。, 、) and processes one sentence at a time. If no delimiter appears within roughly 32 KiB of a sentence's start, Lindera forces a sentence boundary there anyway and logs a warning, to bound the lattice's memory and CPU cost. Up to the next \n or \t, each sentence continues from the words that end the previous one, so the result is, with few exceptions, the one a single lattice over that text gives (see Sentence Splitting ). The forced cut can affect tokenization at the artificial cut point for pathological delimiter-free input, such as minified text or base64-encoded blobs. Lattice construction : Lindera scans each sentence and looks up all possible words in the dictionary at every position, building a directed acyclic graph (lattice) of candidate segmentations. Cost assignment : Each candidate word has an associated word cost (from the dictionary), and each pair of adjacent words has a connection cost (from the connection cost matrix). Optimal path search : The Viterbi algorithm finds the path through the lattice with the minimum total cost, producing the best segmentation.

36.body: The Viterbi algorithm selects the segmentation path with the minimum total cost. The total cost of a path is the sum of: Word costs : Each word in the dictionary has an associated cost. Lower cost means the word is more likely to appear. Common words tend to have lower costs, while rare words have higher costs. Connection costs : The cost of connecting two adjacent words, determined by the right context ID of the left word and the left context ID of the right word. The algorithm computes: Total cost = sum of word costs + sum of connection costs By minimizing this total cost, Lindera finds the most natural segmentation of the input text.

37.body: The connection cost matrix stores the cost of transitioning from one word to another. It is a two-dimensional matrix indexed by: The right context ID of the preceding word The left context ID of the following word These context IDs encode grammatical information about word boundaries. For example, the connection cost between a noun and a particle is typically low (natural sequence), while the connection cost between two verbs in base form might be high (unnatural sequence). The connection cost matrix is compiled into binary format as part of the dictionary build process and is loaded at runtime for efficient lookup.

374.body: Parameter Type Default Description seed string required Path to the seed lexicon file (CSV format) corpus string required Path to the annotated training corpus charDef string required Path to the character definition file (char.def) unkDef string required Path to the unknown word definition file (unk.def) featureDef string required Path to the feature definition file (feature.def) rewriteDef string required Path to the rewrite rule definition file (rewrite.def) output string required Output path for the trained model file lambda number 1.0 Regularization coefficient, finite and >= 0; 0 disables regularization for every type; with L2, MeCab's -c C is 1 / C, so 1.0 is MeCab's -c 1.0 maxIter number 100 Maximum number of training iterations, 1 or more; training stops earlier once the objective converges (see eta) maxThreads number | undefined undefined Number of threads, 1 or more (undefined = auto-detect CPU cores) regularization string "l2" Regularization type: "l1", "l2" or "elasticnet", in any case ("elastic_net" and "elastic-net" also select Elastic Net), as lindera train --regularization takes it elasticNetL1Ratio number 0.5 L1 ratio of Elastic Net regularization, between 0 and 1; 0 uses only L2, 1 uses only L1; used only with "elasticnet" eta number 5e-5 Tolerance of the convergence test, finite and >= 0: training stops before maxIter once the relative change of the objective stays below it for 3 iterations in a row; 0 disables the test The settings are checked before any file is read: an unknown regularization, or a lambda, elasticNetL1Ratio or eta outside its range, throws an InvalidArg error. To train with v6's default settings (the model still differs from v6's, since the first line search changed in #1290 ), pass regularization: "l1" and lambda: 0.01, and eta: 0 to stop only at maxIter.

380.body:
An integer parameter takes only the values its setting can hold. default_word_cost of Lindera::Metadata.new takes -32768 to 32767, the context IDs 0 to 65535, and the penalties of Lindera::Penalty.new a 32-bit integer. A count or an index takes 0 or more: the thresholds of Lindera::Penalty.new, index of Schema#get_field_name and Token#get_detail, and n of Tokenizer#tokenize_nbest. max_iter and max_threads of Lindera.train take 1 or more. cost_threshold of Tokenizer#tokenize_nbest takes a 64-bit integer. A value outside the range raises a RangeError that names the parameter and the range; an index past the end still returns nil: require 'lindera' begin Lindera::Metadata.new(nil, nil, 100_000, nil, nil, nil, nil, nil)
rescue RangeError => e puts "#{e.class}: #{e.message}" # RangeError: default_word_cost must be an integer between -32768 and 32767, got 100000
end tokenizer = Lindera::Tokenizer.new(Lindera.load_dictionary('embedded://ipadic')) begin tokenizer.tokenize_nbest('東京都', -1, nil, nil)
rescue RangeError => e puts "#{e.class}: #{e.message}" # RangeError: n must be an integer between 0 and 18446744073709551615, got -1
end The float settings of Lindera.train are checked the same way, before any file is read: lambda and eta: take a finite number of 0 or more, and elastic_net_l1_ratio: a number between 0 and 1 (see Training ).

40.body: Lindera provides multiple tokenization modes and supports N-Best analysis for enumerating alternative segmentation candidates.
40.title: Tokenization

400.body:
set_mode(mode) Sets the tokenization mode. mode is a Lindera::Mode : Lindera::Mode.normal -- Standard tokenization (default) Lindera::Mode.decompose(penalty = nil) -- Decomposes compound words into smaller units, with the length penalties of a Lindera::Penalty (the default penalty for nil) A value that is not a Lindera::Mode, such as a mode string ('normal'), a Symbol or nil, raises TypeError. To turn a mode name read at run time into a Mode, use Lindera::Mode.from_str . builder.set_mode(Lindera::Mode.normal)
builder.set_mode(Lindera::Mode.decompose(Lindera::Penalty.new(nil, 0, nil, nil))) set_dictionary(path) Sets the system dictionary path or URI. # Use an embedded dictionary
builder.set_dictionary('embedded://ipadic') # Use an external dictionary
builder.set_dictionary('/path/to/dictionary') set_user_dictionary(uri) Sets the user dictionary URI. builder.set_user_dictionary('/path/to/user_dictionary.csv') set_keep_whitespace(keep) Controls whether whitespace tokens appear in the output. Kept whitespace also stays in the lattice, so the other tokens can differ from those of the default output, which skips whitespace in the lattice as MeCab does. To keep whitespace in the lattice without outputting it, use set_skip_whitespace(false) instead. builder.set_keep_whitespace(true) set_skip_whitespace(skip) Sets whether whitespace is skipped in the lattice. skip has the same meaning as segmenter.skip_whitespace in a configuration file : true -- Skips whitespace, so the words on either side of it connect directly, as MeCab does. false -- Keeps whitespace in the lattice as a node of its own (a whitespace dictionary entry or the SPACE unknown word), as before v7. Whitespace is still dropped from the output. nil -- The default of the dictionary's metadata.json: skipping, except with SudachiDict. Use it to undo an earlier call. A value set here overrides the dictionary's default and a skip_whitespace loaded with TokenizerBuilder.from_file. It has no effect while whitespace tokens are kept (set_keep_whitespace(true)), because kept whitespace always stays in the lattice. Other values count by Ruby truthiness, as in set_keep_whitespace: anything but false and nil turns skipping on. With IPADIC, for example, Google が 新しい reads が as a particle (助詞) by default and as a conjunction (接続詞) with set_skip_whitespace(false). See Segmenter for details. # Keep whitespace in the lattice, as before v7
builder.set_skip_whitespace(false) set_space_penalty(value) Sets the left-space penalty for Korean: a candidate that starts right after whitespace and whose part-of-speech tag normally attaches to the preceding word (particles, endings, ...) gets a cost added. value has the same meaning as segmenter.space_penalty in a configuration file : nil -- The default: the rules the dictionary ships in its metadata.json, if any (ko-dic ships mecab-ko-dic's rules; the other bundled dictionaries ship none). Use it to undo an earlier call. false -- Turns the penalty off. true -- Requires the dictionary's rules; build raises RuntimeError for a dictionary that ships none. A hash with string keys, { 'rules' => [{ 'pos' => [...], 'cost' => n }, ...] } -- Applies these rules instead. A candidate whose first part-of-speech tag is listed in pos gets cost added; the first matching rule wins. A value that is not one of these forms, such as 1, 'false' or { 'rules' => 'JKS' }, raises RuntimeError. A value that cannot be converted raises TypeError: a Symbol (also as a hash key or an element, so write %w[JKS] rather than %i[JKS]), a non-finite Float (NaN or Infinity), an Integer outside the 64-bit range, or an object other than nil, true, false, an Integer, a Float, a String, an Array or a Hash. # Turn the penalty off
builder.set_space_penalty(false) # Explicit rules
builder.set_space_penalty({ 'rules' => [ { 'pos' => %w[EC EF EP ETM ETN VCP XSA XSN XSV], 'cost' => 3000 }, { 'pos' => %w[JC JKB JKC JKG JKO JKQ JKS JKV JX], 'cost' => 6000 } ]
}) [!NOTE] Since v6.1.0, ko-dic applies the left-space penalty by default, as mecab-ko does. For example, 검색 이 잘 된다 reads 이 as the interjection IC; without the penalty, as the subject particle JKS. Call builder.set_space_penalty(false) to turn it off. A tokenizer created directly with Lindera::Tokenizer.new(dictionary, ...) always uses the default, so use TokenizerBuilder to turn it off. Only a ko-dic built by Lindera 6.1.0 or later ships the rules; with a ko-dic from the v6.0.0 release the penalty stays off and true fails until the dictionary is rebuilt. See Segmenter for details. append_character_filter(kind, args) Appends a character filter to the preprocessing pipeline. The args parameter is a hash with string keys. builder.append_character_filter('unicode_normalize', { 'kind' => 'nfkc' }) append_token_filter(kind, args) Appends a token filter to the postprocessing pipeline. The args parameter is a hash with string keys, or nil if the filter requires no arguments. builder.append_token_filter('lowercase', nil) The arguments of set_space_penalty, append_character_filter and append_token_filter may nest arrays and hashes at most 128 levels deep. A deeper value, or one that contains itself, raises ArgumentError.

402.body: Lindera::Tokenizer performs morphological analysis on text.
402.title: Tokenizer

403.body:
Lindera::Tokenizer.new(dictionary, mode = nil, user_dictionary = nil, space_penalty: nil) Creates a tokenizer directly from a loaded dictionary. mode is a Lindera::Mode , as TokenizerBuilder#set_mode takes it; nil (the default) means normal mode, and a value that is not a Lindera::Mode, such as a mode string ('normal'), raises TypeError. user_dictionary is optional. The space_penalty: keyword takes the same values as TokenizerBuilder#set_space_penalty . nil (the default) uses the left-space penalty rules the dictionary ships, so with ko-dic the penalty is on; pass false to turn it off. An invalid setting raises the same errors as set_space_penalty and build. require 'lindera' dictionary = Lindera.load_dictionary('embedded://ipadic')
tokenizer = Lindera::Tokenizer.new(dictionary) # ko-dic without the left-space penalty
ko_tokenizer = Lindera::Tokenizer.new(Lindera.load_dictionary('embedded://ko-dic'), space_penalty: false) With a user dictionary: dictionary = Lindera.load_dictionary('embedded://ipadic')
user_dict = Lindera.load_user_dictionary_for('/path/to/user_dictionary.csv', dictionary)
tokenizer = Lindera::Tokenizer.new(dictionary, Lindera::Mode.normal, user_dict)
403.breadcrumbs: Lindera Ruby » Tokenizer API » Creating a Tokenizer
403.title: Creating a Tokenizer

404.body:
tokenize(text) Tokenizes the input text and returns an array of Token objects. tokens = tokenizer.tokenize('形態素解析') Parameters: Name Type Description text String Text to tokenize Returns: Array<Token> tokenize_surfaces(text) Tokenizes the input text and returns only the token surfaces, as an array of strings. This is the fast path for wakati-style use: no Token objects are created and no morphological details are loaded, so it is significantly faster than tokenize when only the surface strings are needed. The result equals tokenizer.tokenize(text).map(&:surface). surfaces = tokenizer.tokenize_surfaces('形態素解析')
# ["形態素", "解析"] Parameters: Name Type Description text String Text to tokenize Returns: Array<String> tokenize_nbest(text, n, unique, cost_threshold) Returns the N-best tokenization results, each paired with its total path cost. results = tokenizer.tokenize_nbest('すもももももももものうち', 3, false, nil)
results.each do |tokens, cost| puts "#{cost}: #{tokens.map(&:surface).inspect}"
end Parameters: Name Type Description text String Text to tokenize n Integer Number of results to return unique Boolean or nil Deduplicate results (default: false) cost_threshold Integer or nil Maximum cost difference from the best path (default: nil) Returns: Array<Array(Array<Token>, Integer)>
404.breadcrumbs: Lindera Ruby » Tokenizer API » Tokenizer Methods
404.title: Tokenizer Methods

405.body: Lindera::Mode is the tokenization mode that TokenizerBuilder#set_mode and Tokenizer.new take. It is the Ruby counterpart of the Rust lindera::mode::Mode: normal mode, or decompose mode with the Lindera::Penalty it uses.
405.title: Mode

406.body:
Lindera::Mode has no new (Lindera::Mode.new raises TypeError). The following class methods create a mode. Lindera::Mode.normal Returns normal mode. Lindera::Mode.decompose(penalty = nil) Returns decompose mode with penalty, a Lindera::Penalty. nil or no argument uses the default penalty. A value that is not a Lindera::Penalty raises TypeError. Lindera::Mode.from_str(name) Returns the mode named name, as the Rust Mode parses it: 'normal', or 'decompose' with the default penalty. The name is case sensitive; any other name, such as 'Normal', raises RuntimeError with an Invalid mode message. Use it for a mode name read at run time, such as from a setting. require 'lindera' normal = Lindera::Mode.normal
decompose = Lindera::Mode.decompose
no_length_penalty = Lindera::Mode.decompose(Lindera::Penalty.new(nil, 0, nil, 0))
from_setting = Lindera::Mode.from_str('decompose')
406.breadcrumbs: Lindera Ruby » Tokenizer API » Creating a Mode
406.title: Creating a Mode

407.body:
Method Returns Description name String "normal" or "decompose" to_s String Same as name inspect String The name, followed by the penalty for decompose mode penalty Penalty or nil A copy of the penalty of decompose mode; nil for normal mode normal? Boolean true for normal mode decompose? Boolean true for decompose mode == Boolean true if the other value is a Mode with the same name and penalty A mode cannot be changed: it has no setter methods, and penalty returns a copy. == compares the name and the penalty, and returns false for a value of another type, such as the string 'normal'. eql? and hash stay by identity, as the Rust Mode is Eq but not Hash: two equal modes are different Hash keys, and uniq keeps both. mode = Lindera::Mode.decompose(Lindera::Penalty.new(nil, 0, nil, 0))
mode.name # "decompose"
mode.normal? # false
mode.decompose? # true
mode.penalty.kanji_penalty_length_penalty # 0
mode.inspect
# "#<Lindera::Mode: decompose Penalty(kanji_threshold=2, kanji_penalty=0, other_threshold=7, other_penalty=0)>" Lindera::Mode.normal.inspect # "#<Lindera::Mode: normal>"
Lindera::Mode.normal.penalty # nil Lindera::Mode.decompose == Lindera::Mode.from_str('decompose') # true
Lindera::Mode.decompose == mode # false (the penalties differ)
Lindera::Mode.normal == 'normal' # false
407.breadcrumbs: Lindera Ruby » Tokenizer API » Mode Methods
407.title: Mode Methods

408.body: Lindera::Penalty configures the length-based penalty thresholds used by decompose mode segmentation. Pass it to Lindera::Mode.decompose .
408.title: Penalty

409.body:
Lindera::Penalty.new(kanji_penalty_length_threshold, kanji_penalty_length_penalty, other_penalty_length_threshold, other_penalty_length_penalty) All four positional arguments are required, but each may be nil to fall back to its default (shown below). require 'lindera' penalty = Lindera::Penalty.new(2, 3000, 7, 1700)
penalty = Lindera::Penalty.new(nil, nil, nil, nil) # uses all defaults
409.breadcrumbs: Lindera Ruby » Tokenizer API » Creating a Penalty
409.title: Creating a Penalty

410.body:
All properties are read-only (there are no setter methods): Property Type Default Description kanji_penalty_length_threshold Integer 2 Kanji-only surface length above which the penalty applies kanji_penalty_length_penalty Integer 3000 Cost penalty added for kanji-only surfaces longer than the threshold other_penalty_length_threshold Integer 7 Surface length above which the penalty applies for non-kanji-only surfaces other_penalty_length_penalty Integer 1700 Cost penalty added for non-kanji-only surfaces longer than the threshold penalty = Lindera::Penalty.new(nil, nil, nil, nil)
penalty.kanji_penalty_length_threshold # 2
410.breadcrumbs: Lindera Ruby » Tokenizer API » Penalty Properties
410.title: Penalty Properties

411.body:
Pass a Penalty to Lindera::Mode.decompose , and the mode to TokenizerBuilder#set_mode or Tokenizer.new . Without length penalties, decompose mode keeps long words whole: require 'lindera' text = '関西国際空港限定トートバッグ'
penalty = Lindera::Penalty.new(nil, 0, nil, 0) builder = Lindera::TokenizerBuilder.new
builder.set_dictionary('embedded://ipadic')
builder.set_mode(Lindera::Mode.decompose)
p builder.build.tokenize(text).map(&:surface)
# => ["関西", "国際", "空港", "限定", "トートバッグ"] builder.set_mode(Lindera::Mode.decompose(penalty))
p builder.build.tokenize(text).map(&:surface)
# => ["関西国際空港", "限定", "トートバッグ"] dictionary = Lindera.load_dictionary('embedded://ipadic')
tokenizer = Lindera::Tokenizer.new(dictionary, Lindera::Mode.decompose(penalty))
p tokenizer.tokenize(text).map(&:surface)
# => ["関西国際空港", "限定", "トートバッグ"]

411.title: Using a Penalty

412.body: Token represents a single morphological token.
412.title: Token

413.body: Property Type Description surface String Surface form of the token byte_start Integer Start byte position in the original text byte_end Integer End byte position in the original text position Integer Token position index word_id Integer Dictionary word ID details Array<String> Morphological details (part of speech, reading, etc.) Additionally, the predicate method unknown? returns true if the word is not in the dictionary: token.unknown? # => false
413.title: Properties

414.body:
get_detail(index) Returns the detail string at the specified index, or nil if the index is past the last detail. A negative index raises RangeError (see Integer arguments ). token = tokenizer.tokenize('東京')[0]
pos = token.get_detail(0) # e.g., "名詞"
subpos = token.get_detail(1) # e.g., "固有名詞"
reading = token.get_detail(7) # e.g., "トウキョウ" Parameters: Name Type Description index Integer Zero-based index into the details array Returns: String or nil to_h / to_hash Returns the token as a plain Hash keyed by Symbols, keeping each field's natural Ruby type, so it serializes without a custom encoder. to_h and to_hash are the same method. require 'json' data = tokenizer.tokenize('東京')[0].to_h
# {surface: "東京", byte_start: 0, byte_end: 6, position: 0,
# word_id: 12345, is_unknown: false, details: [...]} JSON.generate(tokens.map(&:to_h)) Returns: Hash with the keys :surface, :byte_start, :byte_end, :position, :word_id, :is_unknown, and :details. The structure of details depends on the dictionary: IPADIC : [品詞, 品詞細分類1, 品詞細分類2, 品詞細分類3, 活用型, 活用形, 原形, 読み, 発音] UniDic : Detailed morphological features following the UniDic specification ko-dic / CC-CEDICT / Jieba : Dictionary-specific detail formats
414.breadcrumbs: Lindera Ruby » Tokenizer API » Token Methods
414.title: Token Methods

415.body: Lindera::Schema holds an ordered list of field names and provides lookups between field name and index. It is used by Metadata#dictionary_schema and Metadata#user_dictionary_schema (see Dictionary Management ).
415.title: Schema

416.body:
Lindera::Schema.new(fields) Creates a schema from an array of field names. require 'lindera' schema = Lindera::Schema.new(%w[ surface left_context_id right_context_id cost major_pos reading
]) Lindera::Schema.create_default Returns the built-in default schema: 13 fields matching the IPADIC-style layout (surface, left_context_id, right_context_id, cost, major_pos, pos_detail_1, pos_detail_2, pos_detail_3, conjugation_type, conjugation_form, base_form, reading, pronunciation). schema = Lindera::Schema.create_default
416.breadcrumbs: Lindera Ruby » Tokenizer API » Creating a Schema
416.title: Creating a Schema

417.body:
Method Returns Description fields Array<String> All field names, in order get_all_fields Array<String> Same as fields field_count Integer Total number of fields get_field_index(name) Integer or nil Index of the field named name get_field_name(index) String or nil Field name at index get_custom_fields Array<String> Field names after the four fixed fields (surface, left_context_id, right_context_id, cost) get_field_by_name(name) FieldDefinition or nil Full field definition for name validate_record(record) nil Raises ArgumentError if record does not match the schema to_s String e.g. "Schema(fields=13)" inspect String Full field list schema = Lindera::Schema.create_default schema.field_count # 13
schema.get_field_index('cost') # 3
schema.get_field_name(0) # "surface"
schema.get_custom_fields # ["major_pos", "pos_detail_1", ..., "pronunciation"] field = schema.get_field_by_name('surface')
puts "#{field.index} #{field.name} #{field.field_type}" # 0 surface surface schema.validate_record([ '東京', '1288', '1288', '100', '名詞', '固有名詞', '地域', '一般', '*', '*', '東京', 'トウキョウ', 'トーキョー'
])

field = schema.get_field_by_name('surface') field.index # 0
field.name # "surface"
field.field_type # #<Lindera::FieldType: surface>

42.body: Normal mode performs standard tokenization based on dictionary entries. Compound words that exist as single entries in the dictionary are kept as-is. Example -- tokenizing "関西国際空港限定トートバッグ" in Normal mode: 関西国際空港 | 限定 | トートバッグ The compound noun "関西国際空港" (Kansai International Airport) is preserved as a single token because it exists as one entry in the dictionary.
42.title: Normal mode

420.body:
Lindera::FieldType enumerates the category of a single field. Like FieldDefinition, instances are only obtained from a Schema (via FieldDefinition#field_type) -- there is no public constructor. to_s (and inspect) return one of: "surface" -- surface form (word text) "left_context_id" -- left context ID "right_context_id" -- right context ID "cost" -- word cost "custom" -- any other, dictionary-specific field field = Lindera::Schema.create_default.get_field_by_name('surface')
field.field_type.to_s # "surface"
420.title: FieldType

421.body: Lindera Ruby provides functions for loading, building, and managing dictionaries used in morphological analysis.
421.breadcrumbs: Lindera Ruby » Dictionary Management » Dictionary Management
421.title: Dictionary Management

422.breadcrumbs: Lindera Ruby » Dictionary Management » Loading Dictionaries
422.title: Loading Dictionaries

423.body: Use Lindera.load_dictionary(uri) to load a system dictionary. Download a pre-built dictionary from GitHub Releases and specify the path to the extracted directory: require 'lindera' dictionary = Lindera.load_dictionary('/path/to/ipadic') Embedded dictionaries (advanced) -- if you built with an embed-* feature flag, you can load an embedded dictionary: dictionary = Lindera.load_dictionary('embedded://ipadic')
423.breadcrumbs: Lindera Ruby » Dictionary Management » System Dictionaries
423.title: System Dictionaries

424.body:
User dictionaries add custom vocabulary on top of a system dictionary. Load one for the system dictionary it is used with: require 'lindera' dictionary = Lindera.load_dictionary('/path/to/ipadic')
user_dict = Lindera.load_user_dictionary_for('/path/to/user_dictionary.csv', dictionary) A .csv is built with the system dictionary's metadata and checked against its connection matrix as it is built: a row whose context ID lies outside the matrix raises a RuntimeError that names its CSV line and surface (see Context IDs ). A .bin is loaded as it was built. Lindera.load_user_dictionary(uri, metadata) loads a user dictionary with metadata only. A .csv loaded this way is checked when it is combined with the system dictionary, and the error names the entry by its word id: require 'lindera' dictionary = Lindera.load_dictionary('/path/to/ipadic')
metadata = dictionary.metadata
user_dict = Lindera.load_user_dictionary('/path/to/user_dictionary.csv', metadata) Pass the user dictionary when building a tokenizer: require 'lindera' dictionary = Lindera.load_dictionary('/path/to/ipadic')
user_dict = Lindera.load_user_dictionary_for('/path/to/user_dictionary.csv', dictionary) tokenizer = Lindera::Tokenizer.new(dictionary, Lindera::Mode.normal, user_dict) Or via the builder: require 'lindera' builder = Lindera::TokenizerBuilder.new
builder.set_dictionary('/path/to/ipadic')
builder.set_user_dictionary('/path/to/user_dictionary.csv')
tokenizer = builder.build
424.breadcrumbs: Lindera Ruby » Dictionary Management » User Dictionaries
424.title: User Dictionaries

425.breadcrumbs: Lindera Ruby » Dictionary Management » Building Dictionaries
425.title: Building Dictionaries

426.body:
Build a system dictionary from source files: require 'lindera' metadata = Lindera::Metadata.from_json_file('metadata.json')
Lindera.build_dictionary('/path/to/input_dir', '/path/to/output_dir', metadata) The input directory should contain the dictionary source files (CSV lexicon, matrix.def, etc.). Metadata loaded with Lindera::Metadata.from_json_file keeps the space_penalty rules of the metadata.json, and the built dictionary ships them. For ko-dic this means the left-space penalty stays on by default in the dictionary you build; turn it off per tokenizer with TokenizerBuilder#set_space_penalty(false) (see Tokenizer API ).
426.breadcrumbs: Lindera Ruby » Dictionary Management » System Dictionary
426.title: System Dictionary

427.body:
Build a user dictionary from a CSV file for the system dictionary it is used with: require 'lindera' dictionary = Lindera.load_dictionary('/path/to/ipadic')
Lindera.build_user_dictionary_for('user_words.csv', '/path/to/user_dictionary.bin', dictionary)
user_dict = Lindera.load_user_dictionary_for('/path/to/user_dictionary.bin', dictionary) The CSV is built with the system dictionary's metadata and checked against its connection matrix: a row whose context ID lies outside the matrix raises a RuntimeError that names its CSV line and surface, and no file is written (see Context IDs ). The second argument is the path of the file to write. End it with .bin, since the loaders choose how to load a user dictionary by its extension. Lindera.build_user_dictionary(kind, input_file, output_dir, metadata) builds a user dictionary with metadata only. Despite its name, output_dir is the path of the file to write too, not a directory. The rows are checked when the user dictionary is combined with the system dictionary, and the error names the entry by its word id: require 'lindera' metadata = Lindera::Metadata.from_json_file('metadata.json')
Lindera.build_user_dictionary('ipadic', 'user_words.csv', '/path/to/user_dictionary.bin', metadata) The metadata parameter is optional. When omitted, default metadata values are used: Lindera.build_user_dictionary('ipadic', 'user_words.csv', '/path/to/user_dictionary.bin', nil) [!NOTE] The first argument (kind, 'ipadic' above) is currently unused -- it is reserved for future use and has no effect on the build. Any string value can be passed for it today. To build for a system dictionary, use Lindera.build_user_dictionary_for.
427.breadcrumbs: Lindera Ruby » Dictionary Management » User Dictionary
427.title: User Dictionary

433.body: Lindera Ruby supports a composable text processing pipeline that applies character filters before tokenization and token filters after tokenization. Filters are added to the TokenizerBuilder and executed in the order they are appended. Input Text --> Character Filters (preprocessing) --> Tokenization --> Token Filters (postprocessing) --> Output Tokens [!NOTE] This page shows a few commonly used filters as examples -- it is not the complete list. See Filters for the full, authoritative catalogue of every character and token filter that lindera-analysis ships, including parameters and examples.
433.breadcrumbs: Lindera Ruby » Text Processing Pipeline » Text Processing Pipeline
433.title: Text Processing Pipeline

434.body: Character filters transform the input text before tokenization.
434.breadcrumbs: Lindera Ruby » Text Processing Pipeline » Character Filters
434.title: Character Filters

435.body:
Applies Unicode normalization to the input text. require 'lindera' builder = Lindera::TokenizerBuilder.new
builder.set_dictionary('embedded://ipadic')
builder.append_character_filter('unicode_normalize', { 'kind' => 'nfkc' })
tokenizer = builder.build Supported normalization forms: "nfc", "nfkc", "nfd", "nfkd".

Resolves Japanese iteration marks (odoriji) into their full forms. builder = Lindera::TokenizerBuilder.new
builder.set_dictionary('embedded://ipadic')
builder.append_character_filter('japanese_iteration_mark', { 'normalize_kanji' => true, 'normalize_kana' => true
})
tokenizer = builder.build
