810.body:
Japanese text spells the dash and the tilde in two ways each: the dash as ― (U+2015, HORIZONTAL BAR) or — (U+2014, EM DASH), the tilde as ～ (U+FF5E, FULLWIDTH TILDE) or 〜 (U+301C, WAVE DASH). Up to v6.2.0, the dictionary builder rewrote ― to — and ～ to 〜 in every entry of IPADIC and IPADIC-NEologd, whose metadata.json turned the rewrite on with normalize_details. It rewrote the surface, the spelling under which the segmenter finds the entry in the text, and the detail fields, such as the base form and the reading. The text to segment was not rewritten, so an entry that the dictionary source spells with ― or ～ matched only text that spelled it with — or 〜. The rewrite was a workaround for an old EUC-JP conversion. The dictionary sources are UTF-8 now, and ― is the dash that the common Shift_JIS and EUC-JP converters produce and that Aozora Bunko texts use. v7.0.0 keeps every entry as written in the dictionary's CSV files, as MeCab does: Input (dictionary) v6 v7 (as MeCab) ＣＤ―ＲＯＭ (IPADIC) ＣＤ, ― and ＲＯＭ ＣＤ―ＲＯＭ (名詞,一般) ―― (IPADIC) An unknown noun (名詞,サ変接続) 記号,一般 あいいれなぁ～い (IPADIC-NEologd) あいいれなぁ, ～ and い あいいれなぁ～い (形容詞,自立) CD―ROM (IPADIC-NEologd) CD, ― and ROM CD―ROM (名詞,一般) ＣＤ—ＲＯＭ (IPADIC) ＣＤ—ＲＯＭ (名詞,一般) ＣＤ, — and ＲＯＭ —— (IPADIC) 記号,一般 An unknown noun (名詞,サ変接続) The detail fields keep the CSV spelling as well: the entry ＣＤ―ＲＯＭ gives the base form ＣＤ―ＲＯＭ, where v6 gave ＣＤ—ＲＯＭ. With dictionaries built from the same sources, the number of lines that Lindera segments and tags exactly as MeCab does rises, on top of the other changes in this guide, from 459 to 503 of 505 paragraphs of Botchan (from 2,690 to 2,744 of its 2,746 sentences) and from 3,377 to 3,581 of 3,587 paragraphs of Kokoro and I Am a Cat , two other novels from Aozora Bunko. The figures are the same with IPADIC and IPADIC-NEologd, and no line that matched before stops matching. Text that writes these characters as — or 〜 no longer finds the entries that it found only through the rewrite: 12 in IPADIC, all spelled with ―, and 1,085 in IPADIC-NEologd, most of them spelled with ～. In the table above, ＣＤ—ＲＯＭ is split and —— is an unknown noun, as in MeCab. IPADIC-NEologd has most of its words with a tilde in both spellings, so text with either tilde still finds them. To have both spellings find the entries, map the text to the dictionary's spelling with the mapping character filter. IPADIC spells all its entries with a dash with ― and all those with a tilde with 〜, so map — to ― and ～ to 〜: lindera tokenize --dict ipadic --char-filter 'mapping:{"mapping":{"—":"―","～":"〜"}}' # Configuration file
character_filters: - kind: mapping args: mapping: "—": "―" "～": "〜" With this filter, ＣＤ—ＲＯＭ is one word and —— is 記号,一般 again, and text with ～ also finds IPADIC's entries with 〜, which it did not in v6 either. The token's surface is the mapped text, such as ＣＤ―ＲＯＭ; its byte offsets point into the original text. Mapping the tilde the other way, 〜 to ～, would hide IPADIC's entries with 〜. With IPADIC-NEologd, a mapping trades words: some of its words exist in only one spelling, 129 only with ― and 85 only with —, 957 only with ～ and 1,813 only with 〜, so mapping one spelling to the other makes text find the words of one and miss those of the other. NFKC normalization (the unicode_normalize character filter) does not fold these characters: it turns ～ into ~ and leaves ―, — and 〜 as they are. User dictionaries were never rewritten and do not change. The change is in the dictionary builder. The embedded dictionaries and the dictionaries that the 7.0.0 CLI fetches with lindera download keep the spellings; a dictionary directory built or downloaded with v6.2.0 or earlier no longer loads (see Dictionary directories must be rebuilt ). UniDic, ko-dic, CC-CEDICT, Jieba and SudachiDict never turned the rewrite on.
810.breadcrumbs: Migration v6 to v7 » Dash and tilde spellings are kept as written
810.title: Dash and tilde spellings are kept as written

811.body: normalize_details turned this rewrite on and did nothing else, so v7.0.0 removes it from the bundled metadata.json files and from the APIs that create or expose dictionary metadata: API Change Rust Metadata::new takes 10 arguments instead of 11 (normalize_details was the ninth), and the Metadata::normalize_details field and the PrefixDictionaryBuilderOptions::normalize_details method are gone. For binding authors, lindera_binding::CoreMetadata and CoreMetadata::new change the same way. See Rust API changes in lindera_dictionary Python The normalize_details keyword argument of Metadata, the property and the to_dict() key are gone; passing the keyword raises TypeError Ruby Metadata.new takes 8 positional arguments instead of 9, so passing 9 raises ArgumentError; the normalize_details reader and the to_h key are gone PHP The last argument of the Metadata constructor, normalize_details, the property and the toArray() key are gone; passing the argument raises Error (by name) or ArgumentCountError (as a ninth argument) Node.js The normalizeDetails option of Metadata, the property and the toObject() key are gone; TypeScript rejects the option, and at run time it is ignored WASM No change: its Metadata never exposed the setting A metadata.json that still contains normalize_details, such as one written by v6, loads as before, whether it comes with a built dictionary, is passed to lindera build or is read by a binding; the key is ignored and is not written back.
811.breadcrumbs: Migration v6 to v7 » The normalize_details setting is removed
811.title: The normalize_details setting is removed

812.body:
A dictionary can have several entries with the same surface, the same left and right context IDs and the same cost, which differ only in their details, such as the reading or the base form. Such entries are tied: a path costs the same with any of them, so the order in which the segmenter considers them decides which one it outputs. Up to v6.2.0, Lindera added the dictionary entries that start at a position in reverse order, and the search keeps the earlier of two candidates with equal cost, so the last CSV row of a tied group won. The reverse order came in with v2.1.0, apparently by accident. v7.0.0 outputs the first row, as MeCab does: Input (dictionary) v6 v7 (as MeCab) あいつは狡い (IPADIC) 狡い reads コスイ 狡い reads ズルイ IPADIC's Adj.csv has the two rows in this order: 狡い,19,19,4682,形容詞,自立,*,*,形容詞・アウオ段,基本形,狡い,ズルイ,ズルイ
狡い,19,19,4682,形容詞,自立,*,*,形容詞・アウオ段,基本形,狡い,コスイ,コスイ Tied entries exist for 5,637 surfaces in IPADIC, 90,991 in IPADIC-NEologd, 3,324 in UniDic and 175 in ko-dic. In the Japanese dictionaries, the rows of a tied group never differ in the part of speech, only in fields such as the reading and the base form; in ko-dic, 5 groups also differ in the part of speech. With each tied surface on its own line, the number of surfaces whose full details equal those of MeCab 0.996 rises from 1,607 to 5,637 of 5,637 with IPADIC, from 524 to 3,324 of 3,324 with UniDic, and from 8,205 to 86,319 of 86,464 with IPADIC-NEologd (surfaces with whitespace or control characters left out). The other 145 IPADIC-NEologd surfaces contain 、, which no word spans (see The context is carried across 、 and 。 ), or belong to groups whose rows MeCab reads in another order (see below). With ko-dic, all 175 agree when MeCab's dictionary is built from the CSV files in name order. On running text, the number of lines whose full details equal MeCab's rises, on top of the other changes in this guide, from 7,989 to 8,096 of the 8,100 sentences of UD Japanese GSD and from 3,278 to 3,583 of the 3,587 paragraphs of Kokoro and I Am a Cat with IPADIC, and from 3,394 to 3,571 of the same 3,587 paragraphs with UniDic. No line is segmented differently. In all the texts compared, 15 tokens change their part of speech, all to MeCab's. Most of them are entries of the same surface with different context IDs and costs whose paths happen to cost the same in that sentence, and the same order decides between them: UniDic, for example, now reads 御前 as a pronoun (代名詞) instead of a common noun (名詞,普通名詞,一般), as MeCab does. User dictionaries follow the same rule: among tied user entries, the first row is now chosen instead of the last. A user entry that ties with a system entry is still chosen over it, as in v6. This is the one intended difference from MeCab, which chooses the system entry. Such a tie needs a user entry in the detailed format that copies the context IDs and the cost of a system entry, for example to give a word another reading. An entry in the simple three-column format gets the cost and the context IDs of the dictionary's metadata.json (default_word_cost, default_left_context_id and default_right_context_id: -10000, 0 and 0 for IPADIC), so it practically never ties with a system entry. N-best search uses the same order. In addition, the first N-best result is now always the 1-best segmentation, the output of segment; up to v6 it could be another path when several paths had exactly the same cost. The costs of the N-best results do not change: only results with the same cost can change places, which can also change which of them is cut off at the n-th result. N-best search takes about 3% to 4% more instructions (-N 3); the speed of the 1-best segmentation does not change (within 0.2%). With unique (--nbest-unique), every result is the cheapest path of its word boundaries, and of tied entries it now holds the first CSV row in every result, as the 1-best segmentation does. Up to v6, unique N-best went through the paths in order of cost and kept the first path of each segmentation, which could hold either row of a tied pair, and it went through every path of a segmentation before it reached the next one: a short line whose words have many entries could take tens of seconds and gigabytes. The search now goes over word boundaries, so it does not depend on the number of paths. Again, only results with the same cost can change. MeCab's mecab-dict-index reads the CSV files in the order the file system lists them (readdir order), so for tied groups whose rows are in different files (in IPADIC-NEologd and ko-dic), MeCab's choice depends on the file system, while Lindera reads the files in name order. The change is in the segmenter, not in the dictionary files. There is no setting to restore the v6 behavior.
812.breadcrumbs: Migration v6 to v7 » Tied entries resolve to the first CSV row, as in MeCab
812.title: Tied entries resolve to the first CSV row, as in MeCab

813.body: Two segmentations can reach the same position with exactly the same cost while their last words start at different positions. MeCab keeps the one whose last word starts later: it puts every word at the head of the list of words that end where it ends, so the words that start later come first in that list, and of words of equal cost it keeps the first. Up to v6.2.0, Lindera kept the one whose last word starts earlier. v7.0.0 chooses as MeCab does: Input (dictionary) v6 v7 (as MeCab) 腸窒扶斯 (IPADIC) 腸 / 窒 / 扶斯 腸 / 窒扶 / 斯 にフリーホイールダイオードや (IPADIC) フリーホイールダイオード (one unknown word) フリー / ホイール / ダイオード 家系譜 (UniDic) 家 / 系譜 家系 / 譜 차나 마셔 (ko-dic) 차나 / 마셔 차 / 나 / 마셔 電視台上班 (CC-CEDICT) 電視 / 台 / 上班 電視 / 台上 / 班 二十二年 (Jieba) 二 / 十二 / 年 二十 / 二 / 年 Both segmentations of 腸窒扶斯 cost 28,382. With the Japanese and Korean dictionaries, such ties are rare. The texts compared are Botchan (as one file, as paragraphs and as sentences), the 3,587 paragraphs of Kokoro and I Am a Cat and the 8,100 sentences of UD Japanese GSD, each with IPADIC, IPADIC-NEologd and UniDic, and the 7,759 lines of Sangnoksu with ko-dic: about 54,000 lines in all. 9 of them change, all to MeCab's segmentation, and none moves away from it. In Decompose mode, which MeCab does not have, 0 to 2 lines per text change in the same way. With CC-CEDICT, ties are common, because its costs take few values. CC-CEDICT has no connection costs, and an entry of len characters costs max(-36000, -400 * len ** 1.5) (except the 22 entries made only of Latin letters or only of digits, see CC-CEDICT: unknown words no longer cost less than dictionary words ), so two segmentations into entries of the same lengths cost the same, such as 電視 / 台 / 上班 and 電視 / 台上 / 班. Jieba's costs are trained (see Jieba: costs retrained on UD Chinese GSD ), so ties are rare with it; with the mecab-jieba-0.1.2 dictionary, whose 584,430 entries had 12 distinct costs and 4 context IDs, 1,186 sentences changed. Compared with v7.0.0 changed to keep the earlier-starting word on ties, about a quarter of the 4,997 sentences of UD Chinese GSD change with CC-CEDICT: Dictionary Sentences that change Closer to / farther from the gold segmentation Sentences segmented as MeCab, before → after CC-CEDICT 1,267 634 / 455 (sign test p = 6.5 × 10⁻⁸) 3,694 → 4,951 Jieba 3 1 / 1 4,948 → 4,951 The other sentences that change come neither closer to the gold segmentation nor farther from it, and segmentation F1 rises from 77.94 to 78.30 with CC-CEDICT and stays 88.79 with Jieba. Every sentence that changes costs the same either way. When whitespace is skipped (see Whitespace is skipped in the lattice ), the word that ends later wins first, as in MeCab, which looks the next word up from every position a word ends at: an entry that ends with the space wins over a word that ends before it. One difference from MeCab remains in theory: after skipped whitespace, MeCab keeps a node for every position the previous word can end at, while Lindera keeps one, so two words that start right after the same whitespace and tie through previous words that end at different positions can be chosen differently. This needs an entry that ends with whitespace and an exact tie, and it does not occur in the texts compared. Among words that start at the same position, the order of Tied entries resolve to the first CSV row, as in MeCab still applies, and the first N-best result is still the 1-best segmentation. When the context is carried across 、 or 。, a tie between the words that end the previous sentence resolves the same way, as in one lattice over the line: the word that starts later wins (see The context is carried across 、 and 。 ). The 1-best segmentation takes 0.6% to 0.9% more instructions with IPADIC, IPADIC-NEologd and UniDic, with no measurable change in time, and about 2% more instructions and 2% to 5% more time with ko-dic. N-best search (-N 3) takes about 1% more instructions. The change is in the segmenter, not in the dictionary files. There is no setting to restore the v6 behavior.
813.breadcrumbs: Migration v6 to v7 » Equal-cost segmentations keep the later-starting word, as in MeCab
813.title: Equal-cost segmentations keep the later-starting word, as in MeCab

814.body:
lindera tokenize reads its input line by line. Up to v6.2.0, it removed all the whitespace at both ends of each line before tokenizing it: spaces, tabs, U+3000, U+00A0 and the other Unicode whitespace (str::trim). The library, the language bindings and MeCab do not. v7.0.0 removes only the line terminator (
, or 
) and tokenizes the rest of the line as the library does: Input line (IPADIC) v6 v7 (as MeCab) Two spaces, 東京, a space 東京 at bytes 0-6 東京 at bytes 2-8 U+3000, 東京 東京 at 0-6 U+3000 (記号,空白) at 0-3, 東京 at 3-9 東京, U+3000 東京 at 0-6 東京 at 0-6, U+3000 (記号,空白) at 6-9 U+00A0, 東京, U+00A0 東京 at 0-6 U+00A0 (unknown, 記号,一般) at 0-2, 東京 at 2-8, U+00A0 at 8-10 Spaces and tabs are SPACE characters, which the segmenter skips and drops from the output, so they still give no tokens; only the byte offsets of the tokens after them change, and now index the input line, as the library's offsets do. U+3000 at the start or end of a line is a token, as in the middle of a line, with IPADIC, IPADIC-NEologd (記号,空白) and UniDic (空白) (see Dictionary entries with whitespace are kept ). In the 538 lines of Botchan as one file, where 202 lines start with an indent of U+3000, 206 such tokens appear and no other token changes. Text without whitespace at the ends of its lines, such as the 8,100 sentences of UD Japanese GSD and the 3,587 paragraphs of Kokoro and I Am a Cat , gives the same output as before. With --keep-whitespace, the spaces at the start and end of a line are tokens too: two spaces, 東京 and a space give three tokens. With -N, a line of spaces or tabs and an empty line give one result without tokens (NBEST 1 and EOS), as in MeCab, instead of no result (see N-best results cover the whole input for the empty input). The costs of a line with U+3000 at an end include that token. The wakati format writes a line for every input line, or for every result with -N: a line without tokens, such as an empty line or a line of spaces, gives an empty line, as in MeCab. v6 wrote nothing for it, so the output had fewer lines than the input ( Botchan as one file: 505 output lines for its 538 input lines, 33 of them empty). The  of a line that ends with 
 is removed, and only that one . MeCab removes only the 
 and outputs the  as an unknown word; Lindera removes it so that text with Windows line endings does not end every line with a  token. The library and the language bindings never trimmed their input, so they do not change, except for the N-best result of an empty input. The change is in the CLI, not in the dictionary files. No option restores the v6 behavior; to get the v6 offsets and tokens, remove the whitespace at the ends of each line before passing the text to lindera tokenize.
814.breadcrumbs: Migration v6 to v7 » lindera tokenize removes only the line terminator and writes every line
814.title: lindera tokenize removes only the line terminator and writes every line

815.body: Up to v6.2.0, TokenizerBuilder.build() in the WASM binding ignored part of the builder's configuration, depending on how the dictionary was set: Dictionary set with Ignored up to v6.2.0 setDictionaryInstance(), such as a dictionary loaded from OPFS with loadDictionaryFromBytes() setKeepWhitespace(), appendCharacterFilter() and appendTokenFilter() setDictionary(), such as an embedded:// dictionary The user dictionary set with setUserDictionaryInstance() v7.0.0 applies every setting and the user dictionary either way, as the Tokenizer API page describes. For example, with IPADIC loaded from bytes, setKeepWhitespace(true) and the unicode_normalize (NFKC) and lowercase filters turn Ｌｉｎｄｅｒａ 東京 into lindera, a space and 東京; v6 gave Ｌｉｎｄｅｒａ and 東京. With a dictionary instance, build() now also checks what it checks for a dictionary set by URI: unless whitespace is kept, the dictionary's char.def must define the SPACE category. Every bundled dictionary does; a custom dictionary without it now needs setKeepWhitespace(true). The other bindings, the CLI and the library do not change, and neither do the dictionary files. No option restores the v6 behavior; to get it, leave out the settings that v6 ignored.
815.breadcrumbs: Migration v6 to v7 » WASM: the builder settings apply whichever way the dictionary is set
815.title: WASM: the builder settings apply whichever way the dictionary is set

816.body: Up to v6.2.0, the PHP binding read a value of the wrong type for an optional parameter as null, so the call silently used the default, with or without strict_types. For example, $tokenizer->tokenizeNbest('東京都', 2, 'yes') returned results that were not deduplicated, and Lindera\Trainer::train(..., max_iter: $argv[1]) trained for the default 100 iterations whatever the command line said. A required parameter already rejected such a value. v7.0.0 rejects it for the optional parameters too: those of the Penalty, Metadata, FieldDefinition and Tokenizer constructors, of Mode::decompose(), Tokenizer::tokenizeNbest(), Trainer::train(), Trainer::export() and Dictionary::buildUser(). The call throws a TypeError, Invalid value given for argument followed by the parameter's name. A required parameter now throws the same TypeError for such a value; v6 threw an Exception with the same message. null and leaving the argument out still select the default. $lambda of Trainer::train() now takes an int as well as a float, as a PHP float parameter does; v6 read an int there as null too. Pass each argument its declared type, and cast values that arrive as strings, such as (int) $argv[1] (see Argument types ). Code that catches such a value with catch (Exception $e) must catch TypeError instead: a TypeError is an Error, not an Exception. The parameters declared mixed, the other bindings, the CLI and the library do not change. No option restores the v6 behavior.
816.breadcrumbs: Migration v6 to v7 » PHP: optional arguments reject a value of the wrong type
816.title: PHP: optional arguments reject a value of the wrong type

817.body: Up to v6.2.0, the PHP, Node.js and WASM bindings converted an integer argument to the type of its setting by wrapping, so a value outside the range silently became another value. The PHP binding took every int as a 64-bit integer and cast it to the narrower type. In Node.js and WASM, the conversion from a JS number to a 32-bit integer (ECMAScript's ToUint32 or ToInt32) wrapped it before the binding saw it, and a WASM BigInt was taken modulo 2^64. Call v6.2.0 v7.0.0 PHP new Lindera\Metadata(default_word_cost: 100000) cost -31072 ValueError Node.js new Metadata({ defaultLeftContextId: 2 ** 32 + 5 }) context ID 5 Error with the code InvalidArg Node.js schema.getFieldName(2 ** 32) "surface", the first field null WASM new Penalty(-1) threshold 4294967295 a thrown string tokenizeNbest('東京', -1) in PHP, Node.js and WASM all 33 segmentations the binding's error v7.0.0 rejects such a value. The PHP binding throws a ValueError, the Node.js binding an Error with the code InvalidArg, and the WASM binding a string, as for its other errors. The message names the parameter and the range, such as default_word_cost must be an integer between -32768 and 32767, got 100000. The parameters are the integer settings of Metadata (the default word cost and context IDs) and Penalty, the index of FieldDefinition, getFieldName and PHP's Token::getDetail, the number of N-best results and, in Node.js and WASM, the N-best cost threshold, and the iteration and thread counts of the training functions. The checks apply to the constructors and to the property setters (Node.js Metadata, WASM Penalty and FieldDefinition). With them, some values that v6 accepted now throw: A negative index, for which v6 returned null (PHP, Node.js) or undefined (WASM). An index past the end still returns null or undefined. In Node.js and WASM, a number that is not an integer, such as 1.5, NaN or Infinity, which v6 truncated or turned into 0. In WASM, a BigInt cost threshold outside the 64-bit range, and a cost threshold that is not a BigInt. An iteration or thread count of 0 for the training functions, which v6 passed to the trainer: training then failed only after the corpus was read and every lattice was built. The counts take 1 or more, and the Python and Ruby bindings reject 0 too, with a ValueError and a RangeError ( #1275 ). Pass an integer in the range. The TypeScript declarations of the Node.js and WASM bindings do not change. The Python and Ruby bindings already rejected these values, with OverflowError and RangeError, and still do. The RangeError of the Ruby binding now has the message above, which names the parameter and the range, where v6 named only the Rust type (fixnum too big to convert into `i16` ); this covers the N-best cost threshold too, for an Integer outside the 64-bit range. The OverflowError of a Python property setter now names the property in its note (while processing 'default_word_cost' instead of 'cost'). No option restores the v6 behavior.
817.breadcrumbs: Migration v6 to v7 » Bindings: integer arguments outside their range are rejected
817.title: Bindings: integer arguments outside their range are rejected

818.body: Up to v6.2.0, every binding exported a Mode, but no function or constructor took one: set_mode / setMode and the Tokenizer constructors took a mode name, and decompose mode always used the default penalty. Node.js exported a string enum JsMode, whose values 'Normal' and 'Decompose' setMode rejected, and WASM a numeric enum. A custom penalty reached the segmenter only through a configuration file loaded with from_file / fromFile. In Rust, TokenizerBuilder::set_segmenter_mode lost the penalty of a Mode::Decompose the same way, because it wrote only the name of the mode into the configuration. In v7.0.0, the Mode of each binding is a copy of the Rust lindera::mode::Mode: normal mode, or decompose mode with a Penalty. set_mode / setMode and the Tokenizer constructors take a Mode, as set_segmenter_mode and Segmenter::new do in Rust, and no longer take a mode name. Leaving the mode of a constructor out, or passing null / None / nil, still means normal mode, and set_segmenter_mode keeps the penalty: Binding v6 v7 Python builder.set_mode("decompose") builder.set_mode(Mode.decompose(penalty)) Ruby builder.set_mode('decompose') builder.set_mode(Lindera::Mode.decompose(penalty)) PHP $builder->setMode('decompose') $builder->setMode(Lindera\Mode::decompose($penalty)) Node.js builder.setMode("decompose") builder.setMode(Mode.decompose(penalty)) WASM builder.setMode("decompose") builder.setMode(Mode.decompose(penalty)) The Tokenizer constructors take the same Mode as their second argument, for example Tokenizer(dictionary, Mode.normal()) in Python. The penalty is optional: Mode.decompose() uses the default one. With IPADIC and both length penalties 0, decompose mode segments 関西国際空港限定トートバッグ as 関西国際空港 / 限定 / トートバッグ instead of 関西 / 国際 / 空港 / 限定 / トートバッグ. A mode name read at run time, such as a setting, becomes a Mode with Mode.from_str(name) (Mode.fromStr in PHP, Node.js and WASM). It parses the name as the Rust Mode does: "normal" or "decompose", case sensitive, the latter with the default penalty; another name throws the error that set_mode threw for it in v6. A mode name, or any other value that is not a Mode, passed to set_mode / setMode or a constructor now throws a type error: TypeError in Python, Ruby and PHP, an InvalidArg error in Node.js and expected instance of Mode in WASM. The other changes: The Mode classes : a Mode has no constructor; Mode.normal(), Mode.decompose() and Mode.from_str() create one. It has a name, a penalty (a copy, or none for normal mode), the normal and decompose checks, and equality of the name and the penalty (==, or equals() in Node.js and WASM). Python's Mode(mode_str) and its attributes Mode.Normal / Mode.Decompose, Ruby's Lindera::Mode.new, PHP's new Lindera\Mode(), Node.js's JsMode and WASM's Mode.Normal / Mode.Decompose are gone. The Python and Ruby constructors accepted "Normal" and "Decompose", and PHP's any case; from_str does not. A Python Mode is not hashable, as the Rust Mode is not Hash. Node.js : the TypeScript type JsPenalty is renamed Penalty, and its fields become optional; a field left out keeps its default. TypeScript code that names JsPenalty uses Penalty. The package exports no value for the type, so JavaScript code does not change. Rust : TokenizerBuilder::set_segmenter_mode with a Mode::Decompose whose penalty is not the default now applies that penalty, so the output changes. A mode parsed from "decompose", such as the one the CLI's --mode gives, carries the default penalty and is not affected. Binding authors : CoreTokenizerBuilder::set_mode, CoreTokenizer::from_segmenter and CoreTokenizer::from_segmenter_with_space_penalty take a lindera::mode::Mode instead of the &str that v6.2.0's lindera-binding-core took. set_mode no longer returns a Result. lindera_binding::parse_mode parses a mode name, as the bindings' from_str do.
818.breadcrumbs: Migration v6 to v7 » Bindings: a mode is a Mode
818.title: Bindings: a mode is a Mode

819.body: Up to v6.2.0, lindera train built training lattices that differ from those of MeCab's learner: The seed lexicon was not in the lattice, so a gold token competed only with unknown words, never with the other seed words. The unknown-word candidates ignored char.def. A fixed classifier (ASCII digit, ASCII letter, kanji, katakana, hiragana, other) gave the class of the first character, every candidate was one to three characters long, and the class number served as the unk.def entry, so only an unk.def with one entry per class, in the order DEFAULT, HIRAGANA, KATAKANA, KANJI, ALPHA, NUMERIC, worked. Each char.def category got one label, with the feature string of its last unk.def line, and lindera export wrote one unk.def line per category. mecab-ipadic's unk.def has 40 lines for 11 categories; they became 11 lines, and the unknown ALPHA, HIRAGANA and KATAKANA words all became 感動詞, the feature of the last line of each of these categories. A gold token that was not a seed word got an unknown-word label through a check written for IPADIC features (名詞,一般 and the like), or a label without features. An unk.def line with fewer than five fields was silently skipped. When regularization left no bigram weight for some context IDs, lindera export wrote a matrix.def smaller than the IDs of the entries (0 0 when no weight was left at all), and the built dictionary panicked at tokenization. model_info.connection_matrix_size in metadata.json was a square of the larger ID. lindera export wrote 32767 (i16::MAX) to matrix.def for a connection without a trained weight, whose bigram features never met in training or whose weights regularization zeroed. Training gives such a connection the cost 0, and so does MeCab's mecab-dict-gen, so the built dictionary avoided transitions that the model had learned to be neutral. In a five-fold cross-validation with mecab-ipadic's files and v6's default regularization, L1 with --lambda 0.01, writing 0 raised the boundary F1 from 0.9552 to 0.9572 in every fold ( #1168 ). model_info.training_iterations in metadata.json was the --max-iterations value, not the number of iterations that ran. Training stopped at --max-iterations unless one of argmin's own tests held: a gradient norm below the square root of the machine epsilon, or an iteration that left the objective unchanged. With an objective in the hundreds or thousands the first practically never holds, so training ran to the cap. An L2 run whose line search failed panicked ( #1167 ). The export functions of the Python, Node.js, Ruby and PHP bindings wrote lex.csv, matrix.def, unk.def, metadata.json and a fixed char.def with the categories DEFAULT, HIRAGANA, KATAKANA, KANJI, ALPHA and NUMERIC, not the char.def the model was trained with, and no feature.def, rewrite.def, left-id.def or right-id.def. The seed lexicon was read line by line and split on ,, and a line that starts with # was skipped as a comment. mecab-ko-dic's quoted comma surface "," became the surface ", and lindera export wrote it unquoted, so lindera build read the rest of lex.csv as one field and dropped every row after it without an error. The # rows of UniDic, SudachiDict and IPADIC NEologd were not trained. A feature was split on , for the rewrite rules, the feature templates, unknown-word matching and the context IDs of user lexicon entries. A quoted column with a comma in it became several columns and shifted the columns after it: in 19,955 rows of mecab-jieba's training seed, whose quoted English definition is followed by four more columns, %F[6] to %F[9] were pieces of the definition. A %F[n], %L[n] or %R[n] without ? that read past the last column of a feature read * there, so the template still gave a feature, such as U09:*, which every feature with fewer columns shared. MeCab's learner skips the template. The unk.def features of mecab-jieba have five columns, and its feature.def reads %F[6] to %F[9], so its 11 unknown-word labels had four features, U06:* to U09:*, that no seed row had. Model::write_dictionary gave an entry of the user lexicon that Model::read_user_lexicon reads whose context IDs and cost are 0,0,0 the context IDs of another user lexicon entry: the one at the index of the seed row whose feature is the most similar to the entry's, or else the first one. An entry whose feature had no column in common with any seed row got the index of its first character's category in char.def as both IDs, which is not a context ID. Model::write_dictionary gave every such entry with 0,0,0 the same cost, tocost(0.8, cost_factor), whatever its feature. Model::read_user_lexicon read an empty context ID or cost, and a value that is not a number, as 0, and a negative context ID wrapped around to 16 bits (-1 became 65535); the parameters were filled in only when all three were 0. So an entry with an empty cost and given context IDs got the cost 0, and one with empty context IDs and a given cost got the BOS/EOS IDs 0,0. v7.0.0 trains as MeCab's learner does (see How training works ): The lattice has the seed words that start at each position, and the unknown words that the runtime creates there, with the same code: those of the character's default category, with its INVOKE, GROUP and LENGTH settings, for every unk.def entry of the category. Every unk.def line is an entry and a CRF label of its own, with the ID of its category as %t, and lindera export writes every line, in file order. Comment lines and empty lines are skipped, and a line with fewer than five fields is an error. A gold token gets the label of the first seed row with the same span and the same whole feature string; else that of the first unk.def entry of an unknown-word candidate with the same span whose feature columns other than * all equal the gold token's; else a virtual label, which is trained and not exported, as MeCab's learner adds a virtual node. lindera train prints the counts in a Lattice statistics: line, and warns on stderr when no gold token is a seed word, or fewer than half of the gold tokens whose surface has seed rows are, with the first gold token whose surface has seed rows but none with its feature string. matrix.def covers every context ID, plus 0 for BOS/EOS, and model_info.connection_matrix_size gives its size, rows by columns. A connection without a trained weight costs 0 in matrix.def, as in training and in MeCab. model_info.training_iterations is the number of L-BFGS iterations that ran: --max-iterations when that stopped training, fewer when it converged earlier. Training also stops once the relative change of the objective has stayed below --eta (Trainer::eta; default 0.00005, the default of MeCab's learner) for 3 iterations in a row; --eta 0 turns the test off. The bindings use the default. lindera train prints why the optimizer stopped, with the number of iterations and of evaluations of the loss and its gradient, and warns on standard error when an iteration left the objective unchanged or the line search failed far from the optimum. Near the optimum, where which of the two happens depends on the platform, it reports that training converged ( #1300 ). An L2 run whose line search fails keeps the best weights of the run. The export functions of the Python, Node.js, Ruby and PHP bindings write the files lindera export writes, with the same code: the char.def, feature.def and rewrite.def the model was trained with, and left-id.def and right-id.def too. model.dat has the format version 3.0.0. lindera export and the bindings' export functions reject a model.dat of any other version, including every model.dat written by v6.2.0 or earlier, with an error that ends in "re-run lindera train to regenerate it". The seed lexicon is read as CSV, as lindera build reads lex.csv (see Seed Lexicon ): a field may be quoted, a line that starts with # is a row, and the feature columns are kept as written. A quoted field that spans lines is an error. lindera export quotes a surface that contains ,, " or a line break. The user lexicon that Model::read_user_lexicon reads is read the same way. A feature is split into columns as MeCab's learner splits it (see Seed Lexicon ): a quoted column is one column, spaces and tabs before a column are skipped, and the text from a closing quote to the next , is dropped. The rewrite rules join the columns they rewrite with ,, quoting a column that contains , or ", as MeCab does. A template that reads past the last column of a feature gives no feature for it, with or without ?, as in MeCab's learner (see Feature Template ). In the training files of mecab-ipadic, mecab-ipadic-neologd, unidic-mecab, mecab-ko-dic, mecab-jieba and resources/training/, only the unk.def lines of mecab-jieba have features that a template reads past the last column of, so only a model trained on mecab-jieba's files changes. Model::write_dictionary fills in the parameters of a user lexicon entry separately, as mecab-dict-index does: an empty cost is computed, and when either context ID is empty or negative, both are inferred. 0,0,0 still fills in all three. A context ID or cost that is neither empty nor a number in its range is an error that names the entry. A computed cost is the one MeCab's calcCost computes: the sum of the trained weights of the entry's unigram features, converted as the costs of lex.csv are, so an entry whose feature and first character's category are those of a seed row gets that row's cost. Inferred context IDs are those that lex.csv gives the seed row whose feature is the most similar to the entry's. An entry whose feature has no column in common with any seed row is an error, and nothing is written, as mecab-dict-index fails for a user dictionary entry whose feature has no context ID. Every lattice now has the seed words. On the mecab-ipadic data of #1110 , the new default, L2 with --lambda 1.0 (MeCab's -c 1.0), converges in about as many iterations as MeCab's learner (see lindera train regularizes with L2 by default ), where v6's L1 with --lambda 0.01 still reaches --max-iterations ( #1167 ); training there takes about twice as long as MeCab's learner, about two thirds of it outside the optimizer: before it starts ( #1263 ) and after it stops. The files in resources/training/ now define a SPACE category in char.def and a SPACE line in unk.def, so a dictionary trained from them tokenizes without --keep-whitespace, which it needed in v6 ( #1166 ). What you do: train every model again with the 7.0.0 lindera train or the bindings' training functions, then export it and build the dictionary again. Give every unk.def line at least five fields. An unk.def with several entries per category, such as mecab-ipadic's, is now trained and exported as it is. Remove the comment lines from your seed lexicons: a line that starts with # is now a row. Give the context IDs of a user lexicon entry whose feature has no column in common with any seed row. Write each context ID and cost of a user lexicon entry as a number, or leave it empty to have it filled in. There is no setting to restore the v6 behavior.
819.breadcrumbs: Migration v6 to v7 » lindera train builds its lattices as MeCab's learner does
819.title: lindera train builds its lattices as MeCab's learner does

820.body: lindera train, Trainer::new of lindera_trainer and lindera_crf, and the training functions of the Python, Node.js, Ruby and PHP bindings regularize with L2 and a coefficient of 1.0 by default: the objective of MeCab's learner with its default -c 1.0 ( #1261 ). v6 used L1 with 0.01, and lindera_crf::Trainer::new L1 with 0.1. MeCab's learner adds ‖w‖² / (2C) to the loss, so the coefficient, --lambda, is 1 / C in general (-c 0.5 is --lambda 2.0); its help no longer gives it the range 0.0 to 1.0, which was never enforced. The new constant DEFAULT_LAMBDA of lindera_trainer and lindera_crf holds the default. On a five-fold cross-validation with mecab-ipadic's files ( #1110 ), with the default cap of 100 iterations, means over the folds: Regularization Iterations Boundary F1 Span + POS (4 columns) F1 matrix.def L2, --lambda 1.0 (v7's default) 77 to 82, converged 0.9613 0.9397 18.9 MB L1, --lambda 0.01 (v6's default) 100, the cap 0.9578 0.9350 8.3 MB L2, --lambda 0.01 (--lambda 0.01 only) 100, the cap 0.9582 0.9361 19.0 MB L1, --lambda 1.0 (--regularization l1 only) 100, the cap 0.9605 0.9380 3.3 MB MeCab's learner, -c 1.0 75 to 83 evaluations, converged 0.9611 0.9398 22.5 MB (fold 0) lindera export gives labels with equal weights one context ID. L1 sets many weights to 0, so many labels share an ID; L2 sets none to 0, and its matrix.def there has about 1,200 by 1,200 IDs, close to the 1316 by 1316 of mecab-ipadic's own. The built dictionary is 4.0 % larger than with v6's default settings there (fold 0). On resources/training/, training stops after 8 iterations instead of 15, and the exported unk.def gets other context IDs and costs; the tokenize output in the docs does not change. These numbers include the first line search of lindera train starts its first line search at a unit step . What you do: to use v6's default settings, give both. A setting given alone keeps its value, and the other one takes the new default: v6 invocation Meaning in v7 To use v6's settings No regularization flag L2, --lambda 1.0 --regularization l1 --lambda 0.01 --lambda X only L2, --lambda X Add --regularization l1 --regularization l1 only L1, --lambda 1.0 Add --lambda 0.01 Both Unchanged — The model still differs from v6's, since the first line search starts at another step (see the next section). To stop as v6 did, also pass --eta 0 (see lindera train builds its lattices as MeCab's learner does ). In Rust, call .use_l2(false).regularization_cost(0.01) on lindera_trainer::Trainer::new(config)?, and .regularization(Regularization::L1, 0.1)? on lindera_crf::Trainer::new(). The bindings take the type, the Elastic Net ratio and eta as the CLI does ( #1262 ): pass regularization="l1", lambda_=0.01 in Python, regularization: "l1", lambda: 0.01 in Node.js, a lambda of 0.01 and regularization: 'l1' in Ruby, and regularization: 'l1', lambda: 0.01 in PHP. A model records the type, and the Elastic Net ratio, next to the coefficient: in model.dat and as regularization_type and elastic_net_l1_ratio in the model_info of the exported metadata.json ( #1272 ). A lambda that is NaN or infinite is now rejected: lindera train and lindera_crf::Trainer::regularization fail with `lambda must be finite and = 0`, where v6 accepted it, and the bindings raise before they read any file ( #1262 ).

820.title: lindera train regularizes with L2 by default

821.body: The first line search of the L-BFGS and OWL-QN optimizers of lindera train, of Trainer in lindera_trainer and lindera_crf, and of the training functions of the Python, Node.js, Ruby and PHP bindings starts at a step of 1 / |d|, d being the first search direction, so that its first trial point lies at unit distance from the initial weights, as in MeCab's learner and libLBFGS; every later one starts at a step of 1, as before ( #1290 ). v6 started the first one at 1 too, so its first trial point lay as far from the initial weights as the gradient was long: 1.1e5 on the corpus of #1260 , where, with L1 and --lambda 0.01, the first search went so far that the loss became rounding error and training stopped with "no progress" after 3 iterations. It now converges after 53. Every trained model changes, with every regularization type. On the cross-validation of the previous section, the accuracy stays within the spread between folds, and the first line search takes 1 evaluation instead of about 7 with L2 and 13 with L1 (means over the folds, the same build with each first step): Regularization First step Iterations Evaluations Boundary F1 Span + POS (4 columns) F1 L2, --lambda 1.0 1 84.4 94.2 0.9613 0.9398 L2, --lambda 1.0 1 / |d| 79.4 83.8 0.9613 0.9397 L1, --lambda 0.01 1 100 113.8 0.9572 0.9344 L1, --lambda 0.01 1 / |d| 100 101.4 0.9578 0.9350 L1, --lambda 1.0 1 100 112.8 0.9607 0.9381 L1, --lambda 1.0 1 / |d| 100 101.2 0.9605 0.9380 Elastic Net, --lambda 1.0 1 97.6 110.4 0.9614 0.9393 Elastic Net, --lambda 1.0 1 / |d| 98.8 100.0 0.9612 0.9391 What you do: nothing. With v6's settings (see the previous section), a model is no longer v6's byte for byte.

821.title: lindera train starts its first line search at a unit step

822.body: Up to v6.2.0, lindera build accepted a lex.csv row or an unk.def line whose context IDs fall outside matrix.def, and the built dictionary panicked when such a word was looked up during tokenization. A matrix.def row whose ID exceeded its axis was accepted too, and its cost landed in another cell. v7.0.0 rejects all of these, as MeCab's mecab-dict-index does: in every lex.csv row and unk.def line, the right context ID must be below the first value of the matrix.def header, and the left context ID below the second. The error names the file, the line, the ID and the matrix size: Error: LinderaError { kind: Content, source: ./dict-source/lex.csv: line 2: right context id 2 is out of range for the connection matrix (matrix.def size 2 2; right context ids must be below 2) } A dictionary whose metadata.json sets skip_invalid_cost_or_id drops such a lex.csv row instead, with a warning, which the CLI writes to standard error (see The CLI writes library warnings to standard error ). unk.def lines are always checked. An unk.def line with fewer than four fields, such as a comment or an empty line, is an error instead of a panic, also in DictionaryBuilder::build_unknown_dictionary and parse_unk of lindera_dictionary. The error names the line, and so does the error for a context ID or a cost that is not a number, which did not name it before. A user dictionary is checked when it is combined with the system dictionary: Segmenter::try_new, the configuration path, lindera tokenize --user-dict, and the Tokenizer constructors and builders of the language bindings return an error that names the first entry outside the matrix ( #1171 ; see Context IDs ). Segmenter::new does not check, as before. lindera build --user checks the rows already when the new --system-dict option names the system dictionary (DictionaryBuilder::with_system_matrix in the Rust API), and names the first row outside the matrix by its CSV line and surface ( #1182 ). A .csv user dictionary that the configuration path, lindera tokenize --user-dict or the bindings' TokenizerBuilder loads by path, or that the new load_user_dictionary_for of the Rust API loads, is checked the same way as it is built for the system dictionary, and its error names the CSV line and surface too ( #1187 ). The language bindings have such a loader for a loaded system dictionary too: load_user_dictionary_for in Python and Ruby, loadUserDictionaryFor in Node.js, Lindera\Dictionary::loadUserFor in PHP and loadUserDictionaryFromBytesFor in WebAssembly ( #1193 ). The loaders that take metadata are unchanged. The user dictionary builders of these bindings have such a variant as well, which checks the rows against a loaded system dictionary as it builds the CSV: build_user_dictionary_for in Python and Ruby, buildUserDictionaryFor in Node.js and Lindera\Dictionary::buildUserFor in PHP ( #1188 ). The builders that take metadata are unchanged too: their output_dir is, as before, the path of the file they write, not a directory. The errors for a user dictionary row whose cost or context ID is not a number, from lindera build --user or from loading a .csv user dictionary, name the row's CSV line (at line 1). Before, they counted the rows in the order of their surfaces (at row 2 for a row on line 1 whose surface sorts second). Dictionaries that mecab-dict-index builds pass, since it checks the same bounds. A dictionary exported by lindera export of v6.2.0 or earlier can fail, since its matrix.def could be smaller than its context IDs; train and export it again with 7.0.0 (see the previous section). For another dictionary that fails, fix the IDs in lex.csv or unk.def or the size in matrix.def.

822.title: lindera build rejects context IDs outside the connection matrix

823.body: Up to v6.2.0, lindera build and lindera train accepted a char.def and an unk.def that MeCab's mecab-dict-index rejects ( #1195 ): A range line of char.def that names a category no line defines. The built dictionary panicked on a character of the category, and so did training when the corpus had one. A range line before the definition of its category, or a category defined twice. The categories defined after it got the INVOKE, GROUP and LENGTH settings of another category, which changed the unknown words. A char.def category without an unk.def line. A character of it that no word covers got no unknown word, so tokenization stopped its output before it, without an error, and a training lattice had no path through it. An unk.def line whose category char.def does not define. The line was never used, and lindera export wrote it back. v7.0.0 rejects all of these, as mecab-dict-index does. The error names the file, the category and, except for a category without an unk.def line, the line. For example, with 0x3005 KANJI_ITERATION on line 8 of char.def, whose category no line defines: Error: LinderaError { kind: Content, source: ./dict-source/char.def: line 8: category KANJI_ITERATION is not defined; a range line can only name a category defined on an earlier line } lindera train and the bindings' training functions check their input in the same way before they train, and number the unk.def lines as in the file, comment and empty lines included. Every bundled dictionary passes, and so does a dictionary that mecab-dict-index builds. For another dictionary that fails, define each category once, before the range lines that name it, give every category at least one unk.def line, and remove the unk.def lines of categories that char.def does not define.
823.breadcrumbs: Migration v6 to v7 » lindera build and lindera train check char.def against unk.def
823.title: lindera build and lindera train check char.def against unk.def

824.body: Up to v6.2.0, lindera build gave a cell that matrix.def does not list the cost 32767 (i16::MAX), which made the connection very expensive. MeCab's mecab-dict-index gives such a cell the cost 0, and v7.0.0 does the same ( #1211 ; see Cells missing from matrix.def ). The matrix.def of every bundled dictionary lists every cell, and so does the matrix.def that lindera export writes, so neither changes. A dictionary built from a matrix.def that leaves cells out can segment differently, since a connection through such a cell now costs 0. To keep a connection expensive, list its cell with a cost.
824.breadcrumbs: Migration v6 to v7 » lindera build gives a cell missing from matrix.def the cost 0
824.title: lindera build gives a cell missing from matrix.def the cost 0

825.body: Up to v6.2.0, the lindera CLI installed no logger, so the warnings that the Lindera libraries report through the log crate were dropped ( #1107 ). v7.0.0 writes them to standard error, warnings and errors by default. Standard output does not change. For example: lindera tokenize warns when it cuts a sentence because more than 32 KiB of text have no sentence delimiter. lindera build warns when it drops a lex.csv row because of skip_invalid_cost_or_id, and when the dictionary's metadata.json sets connection_id_mapping (ko-dic, UniDic) and --context-id-freq is not given. Pass the context_id_freq.txt of the dictionary crate, as the build examples do. [WARN lindera_segmenter::segmenter] no sentence delimiter (\n, \t, 。, 、) found within 32768 bytes from offset 0; forcing a sentence boundary to bound lattice size (see https://github.com/lindera/lindera/issues/871) The RUST_LOG environment variable selects the messages: RUST_LOG=error hides the warnings, and RUST_LOG=debug adds debugging messages (see Warnings and log messages ). lindera build and lindera train no longer warn about an unk.def line whose left and right context IDs differ, which mecab-dict-index accepts: every line of mecab-ko-dic's unk.def is such a line. Rust programs that install a logger no longer get this warning either.
825.breadcrumbs: Migration v6 to v7 » The CLI writes library warnings to standard error
825.title: The CLI writes library warnings to standard error

826.breadcrumbs: Migration v6 to v7 » Rust API changes in lindera_dictionary
826.title: Rust API changes in lindera_dictionary

827.body: These affect only Rust code that uses lindera-trainer directly or through lindera::dictionary::trainer (the train feature) (see lindera train builds its lattices as MeCab's learner does ): v6 v7 SerializableModel::unk_category_names: Vec<String> and SerializableModel::unk_categories: BTreeMap<String, String> SerializableModel::unk_entries: Vec<(String, String)>, the (category, feature string) pairs of unk.def in file order ModelMetadata::version is "1.0.0", and Model::read_model does not check it "3.0.0"; Model::read_model rejects a model of any other version — New in model: MODEL_FORMAT_VERSION — New: SerializableModel::export, which writes the files of lindera export to a directory TrainerConfig::dict() holds an empty lexicon and a placeholder unknown-word dictionary Holds the seed lexicon (system_lexicon()) and the unk.def entries (unk_handler()) TrainerConfig::from_readers skips an unk.def line with fewer than five fields Returns an error TrainerConfig::from_readers accepts a char.def and an unk.def that mecab-dict-index rejects Returns an error that names the file, the category and, where there is one, the line (see lindera build and lindera train check char.def against unk.def ) Trainer::max_grouping_len(len) bounds the unknown-word candidates, which never exceed three characters Caps unknown-word grouping with the runtime's meaning, in characters beyond the first; None, the default, leaves it unbounded Model::num_labels() and ModelMetadata::label_count count one unknown-word label per char.def category Count one per unk.def entry; the virtual labels are not counted Model::write_left_id_def / write_right_id_def write the IDs of the bigram feature strings, another ID space from the context IDs of lex.csv and matrix.def Write the context IDs, as SerializableModel::write_left_id_def / write_right_id_def write them for the model that Model::write_model writes ModelMetadata::iterations (and model_info.training_iterations) is the max_iter setting The number of L-BFGS iterations that ran ModelMetadata records the regularization coefficient only New: ModelMetadata::regularization_type (a RegularizationType) and ModelMetadata::elastic_net_l1_ratio (Some for Elastic Net only), exported as model_info.regularization_type and model_info.elastic_net_l1_ratio ( #1272 ) — New: Trainer::eta and Trainer::get_eta, the tolerance of the convergence test, and DEFAULT_ETA (5e-5), its default; lindera-crf adds the same Trainer::eta and DEFAULT_ETA, and StopReason with TrainingStats::evaluations and TrainingStats::stop_reason Model::write_connection_costs and SerializableModel::write_connection_costs write i16::MAX for a connection without a trained weight Write 0, the cost the connection has in training and in MeCab Trainer::new regularizes with L1 (use_l2 false) and regularization_cost 0.01 With L2 and DEFAULT_LAMBDA (1.0); use_l2(false) selects L1 (see lindera train regularizes with L2 by default ) — New: DEFAULT_LAMBDA (1.0), the default coefficient; lindera_crf adds the same constant, and its Trainer::new regularizes with Regularization::L2 and it instead of Regularization::L1 and 0.1 — New in lindera_crf: FeatureSet::with_shared_bigrams, which takes the bigram feature IDs as Arc<[Option<NonZeroU32>]> so that labels can share them. FeatureSet holds them this way, which changes the rkyv archive of FeatureSet, FeatureProvider and RawModel; model.dat does not hold them ( #1263 ) FeatureExtractor::unigram_feature_ids, left_feature_ids and right_feature_ids are public HashMap<String, NonZeroU32> fields Private; the methods unigram_feature_ids(), left_feature_ids() and right_feature_ids() return a &FeatureIdMap, new in feature_extractor and read-only: len, is_empty, get, contains_key, resolve (the feature of an ID) and iter, which lists the features in ascending ID order ( #1286 ) TrainerConfig::surface_features() returns a HashMap<String, String> of the seed rows' features by surface Removed; TrainerConfig::features() returns the seed rows' feature strings next to surfaces(), and get_features still returns the feature of the last seed row with the surface ( #1286 ) A model is now written with MODEL_FORMAT_VERSION as its metadata.version, and Model::read_model checks it, in both the rkyv and the legacy JSON format, so a model written by v6.2.0 or earlier has to be trained again. Code that reads unk_category_names or unk_categories reads unk_entries instead: one pair per unk.def line, several per category included, in the order of the exported unk.def. If you set Trainer::max_grouping_len, pass the cap that the dictionary will be used with (max_grouping_len of the segmenter, --max-grouping-len of the CLI). A FeatureIdMap keeps the feature strings in one buffer and only the IDs in its hash table, which takes less memory than a HashMap for the millions of features of a full dictionary; only the extractor adds to it. Code that used surface_features() can build the same map, where the last seed row with a surface wins: let surface_features: HashMap<&str, &str> = config .surfaces() .iter() .map(String::as_str) .zip(config.features().iter().map(String::as_str)) .collect();

827.title: Rust API changes in lindera_trainer

828.body: Users of the language bindings and the CLI : the Python, Node.js, Ruby, PHP, and WASM packages and lindera-cli keep their package names, and their APIs apart from the normalize_details setting of Metadata (see The normalize_details setting is removed ) and, in PHP, optional arguments of the wrong type (see PHP: optional arguments reject a value of the wrong type ), and, in PHP, Node.js and WASM, integer arguments outside their range (see Bindings: integer arguments outside their range are rejected ), and the mode, which they take as a Mode instead of a name, and the Node.js TypeScript type JsPenalty, now Penalty (see Bindings: a mode is a Mode ). The restructuring is internal to the Rust crates. A dictionary directory built or downloaded with v6.2.0 or earlier has to be rebuilt or downloaded again (see Dictionary directories must be rebuilt ); the embedded dictionaries need nothing. A model file trained with v6.2.0 or earlier has to be trained again (see lindera train builds its lattices as MeCab's learner does ), and training regularizes with L2 and a coefficient of 1.0 unless both the type and the coefficient are given (see lindera train regularizes with L2 by default ). The output changes are the IPADIC conjugation fix, which matters only if you read those two fields by name, the whitespace entries, which matter only for text with U+3000 (IPADIC, IPADIC-NEologd, UniDic) or with spaces (SudachiDict), the segmentation of text that contains whitespace, the char.def fix, which matters only for text with Ð, 々 or 〇, the context carried across 、 and 。, which matters only for text with 、 or 。 inside a line, the N-best fix, which matters only for N-best results for input with more than one sentence or for an empty input, the unknown words that start at every position, which matter for runs of katakana, symbols or Latin letters in normal mode, the unknown words made from the default category, which matter for ko-dic hanja numerals followed by hanja and for 〇 with ko-dic, the new costs of CC-CEDICT, which matter for its entries that mix Latin letters or digits with Chinese characters and for its N-best costs, the 〇 entry of Jieba, which matters only for text with 〇, the retrained costs of Jieba, which change the segmentation of most Chinese text with Jieba and the cost of simple Jieba user dictionary words, the dash and tilde spellings, which matter only for text with ―, —, ～ or 〜 with IPADIC or IPADIC-NEologd, the choice among tied entries, which matters only if you read token details such as the reading or the base form, or the order of N-best results with the same cost, the choice between segmentations of equal cost, which changes the segmentation of a few lines with the Japanese and Korean dictionaries and Jieba and of about a quarter of the sentences with CC-CEDICT, in the CLI only, the whitespace at the ends of an input line and the output of lines without tokens, which matter only for lines that start or end with whitespace and for the wakati and N-best output of empty lines and lines of spaces, and the warnings on standard error, which matter only for scripts that read it, and, in the WASM binding only, the builder settings that v6 ignored for one way of setting the dictionary. Projects staying on lindera = "6" : the 6.x releases of lindera and lindera-analysis remain on crates.io and keep working together. Nothing changes until you bump the major version. Users of the segmenter API only : code that uses Segmenter, load_dictionary, Mode, and the other lindera::… items of v6 compiles unchanged with lindera = "7", unless it calls the lattice backtraces of lindera::dictionary::Lattice or creates metadata with lindera::dictionary::Metadata::new (see Rust API changes in lindera_dictionary ). Dictionary directories loaded by path still have to be rebuilt. The default build now also compiles lindera-analysis and its dependencies (kanaria, regex, serde_yaml_ng, unicode-blocks, unicode-normalization, unicode-segmentation); to keep the v6 dependency tree, set default-features = false, features = ["mmap"].
828.breadcrumbs: Migration v6 to v7 » Who does not need to act
828.title: Who does not need to act

829.body: Rust crate users: Bump lindera to "7" and, in the same commit, either bump lindera-analysis to "7" or remove it and import from lindera::analysis::…. Optionally replace lindera_analysis:: with lindera::analysis:: in use paths — both name the same types. If you set default-features = false, add "analysis" (for the Tokenizer and filters) and "mmap" (for memory-mapped loading) to features as needed. Replace features = ["lindera-<dictionary>"] with features = ["embed-<dictionary>"]. Optionally drop a direct lindera-dictionary dependency in favor of lindera::dictionary::core, ::builder, ::viterbi, and the other re-exported modules. If you call Lattice::tokens_offset, tokens_offset_into, nbest_tokens_offset or NBestGenerator::next, destructure (start, end, word_id) and use the returned end instead of the next token's start. If you use the () value of Lattice::tokens_offset_into, for example as the body of a closure, add a ;: it now returns the BOS index of the best path. If you call Metadata::new, delete its ninth argument, normalize_details, and stop using the Metadata::normalize_details field and PrefixDictionaryBuilderOptions::normalize_details. If you build Metadata with a struct literal that lists every field, add skip_whitespace: None or end it with ..Default::default(). If you read CharacterDefinition::lookup_categories, expect the default category first and the others in category id order. If you call UnknownDictionary::gen_unk_words or UnknownDictionary::compatible_unk_index, or use UnkWord or WordIdx, list the unknown words with Lattice::unknown_word_candidates instead. If you read SerializableModel::unk_category_names or unk_categories, read unk_entries instead, and if you set Trainer::max_grouping_len, pass it the cap that the dictionary will be used with. If you pass TokenizerBuilder::set_segmenter_mode a Mode::Decompose whose penalty is not the default, expect that penalty to apply. Binding authors: Depend on lindera-binding instead of lindera-binding-core, and replace lindera_binding_core:: with lindera_binding::. Delete the normalize_details argument of CoreMetadata::new, which now takes 10 arguments, and stop using the CoreMetadata::normalize_details field. If you build CoreMetadata with a struct literal that lists every field, add skip_whitespace: None or end it with ..Default::default(). Pass a lindera::mode::Mode instead of a mode name to CoreTokenizerBuilder::set_mode, which no longer returns a Result, and to CoreTokenizer::from_segmenter and CoreTokenizer::from_segmenter_with_space_penalty; parse a name with lindera_binding::parse_mode. Build environments: Use Rust 1.89 or newer. Rename LINDERA_DICTIONARIES_PATH to LINDERA_BUILD_DICTIONARY_CACHE_DIR in shell profiles, CI configuration, and container images. Everyone who loads a dictionary from files: Rebuild with lindera build, or download again, every dictionary directory made with v6.2.0 or earlier, including those saved in the WASM binding's OPFS storage: v7.0.0 rejects them (format version 3). The embedded dictionaries and user dictionaries need nothing. Users of IPADIC or IPADIC-NEologd: If you read conjugation_type or conjugation_form by name (including the CLI's JSON output), expect the two values to trade places. If you build dictionaries with your own copy of the IPADIC metadata.json, swap the two names in it. Users of IPADIC, IPADIC-NEologd, UniDic or SudachiDict with text that contains U+3000 or spaces: Expect U+3000 to be 記号,空白 (IPADIC) or 空白 (UniDic) tokens, and SudachiDict to segment spaced text much closer to Sudachi. Drop U+3000 with japanese_stop_tags or NFKC normalization if you do not want it. Everyone who segments text that contains whitespace: Expect MeCab's segmentation for such text (most visible with ko-dic; not with SudachiDict, which keeps whitespace in the lattice as Sudachi does). If you need the v6 handling of whitespace, set skip_whitespace(false), "skip_whitespace": false, or --disable-skip-whitespace; the other output changes in this guide still apply. Expect the token of a dictionary entry that ends with a space (in IPADIC-NEologd, ko-dic and SudachiDict) to include that space, as in MeCab. Users of any bundled dictionary with text that contains Ð, 々 or 〇: Expect Ð to stay in the output, and 々 after an unknown kanji to be a token of its own. Users of lindera train: Give every range line of your char.def at least one category. If your char.def has single-code-point or overlapping lines, retrain: the %t feature now follows those lines as MeCab does. Train every model again with the 7.0.0 lindera train (or the bindings' training functions), then export it and build the dictionary again: lindera export rejects a model.dat written by v6.2.0 or earlier, and the training lattices, the unknown-word labels and the exported unk.def and matrix.def have changed. Give every line of your unk.def at least five fields: the category, the two context IDs, the cost and at least one feature column. If your char.def and unk.def were copied from resources/training/ and have no SPACE category, add it as those files now do, so that the trained dictionary tokenizes without --keep-whitespace ( #1166 ). If training reports a category of char.def or unk.def, define each category once, before the range lines that name it, give every category an unk.def line, and remove the unk.def lines of undefined categories ( #1195 ). Expect training to stop before --max-iterations once the objective converges, and read the line lindera train prints to see why it stopped; pass --eta 0 (Trainer::eta(0.0) in Rust) to stop only at the cap and on the optimizer's own tests, as v6 did ( #1167 ). Expect training to regularize with L2 and a coefficient of 1.0 unless you give both the type and the coefficient; pass --regularization l1 --lambda 0.01 (.use_l2(false).regularization_cost(0.01) in Rust) to use v6's default settings. If you pass only --lambda (lambda in the bindings), it is now the L2 coefficient; with --regularization l1 only, the coefficient is 1.0. The bindings take the type as regularization ( #1261 , #1262 ). Expect every trained model to differ from v6's, even with v6's settings, since the first line search starts at a unit step ( #1290 ). Expect a NaN or infinite lambda to be rejected ( #1262 ). Everyone who builds a system dictionary with lindera build: If the build reports a context ID out of range for the connection matrix, fix the IDs in lex.csv or unk.def or the size in matrix.def, or set skip_invalid_cost_or_id to drop such lex.csv rows. Such a dictionary used to build and then panic at tokenization. A dictionary exported by v6.2.0 or earlier is best trained and exported again. If the build reports a category of char.def or unk.def, define each category once, before the range lines that name it, give every category an unk.def line, and remove the unk.def lines of undefined categories ( #1195 ). Everyone who uses a user dictionary with detailed entries: If building the tokenizer reports a user dictionary entry whose context ID is out of range for the connection matrix, fix the IDs in the user dictionary CSV for the system dictionary you use, and build the .bin again if you use one. Such a user dictionary used to panic at tokenization when the entry matched the input. Users of Japanese text with 、 or 。 inside a line: Expect some words after 、 or 。 to be read in the context of the words before them, mostly as MeCab reads them. No setting restores the v6 output. Users of N-best results: Expect every result to cover the whole input, and the results from the second one on to change for input with more than one sentence. For a line with 、 or 。, expect every cost to change, the first result's included: the costs are those of one lattice over the line. If you set a cost threshold, it now applies to the total cost of the whole input, not to each sentence. Expect an empty input to give one result without tokens, as an input of only whitespace does, instead of no result. Expect the first result to be the 1-best segmentation also when several paths have exactly the same cost; results with the same cost can change places. Users of normal mode with text that has runs of katakana, symbols or Latin letters: Expect such runs to be split where MeCab splits them: katakana joined by ・ (IPADIC, IPADIC-NEologd, UniDic), unknown symbols right after a dictionary symbol, and Korean sentence-final punctuation such as .". No setting restores the v6 output, and unknown_word_ladder(false) no longer gives the output of Lindera before v6. Expect katakana- and Latin-heavy text to take about 13% more instructions, and very long katakana runs in N-best to take much more time and memory. Users of ko-dic with text that has hanja numerals or 〇: Expect a ko-dic hanja numeral and the hanja after it to be one unknown word (三國史記 is one SH word), and 〇 to be a symbol (SY), as in MeCab. No setting restores the v6 output. Users of CC-CEDICT: Expect entries that mix Latin letters or digits with Chinese characters, such as T恤 and 卡拉OK, to be one word, and 〇 and entries such as PK to come with their pinyin and definition. Latin words, runs of kana and numbers stay one word, as in v6. Expect the costs of paths, and so N-best costs, to change: unknown words cost 400 instead of −3,200. Build a CC-CEDICT dictionary directory from the CC-CEDICT-MeCab-0.1.0-20261021 archive. Users of Jieba with text that has 〇: Expect each 〇 to be one numeral word (m, pinyin ling2) instead of part of an unknown word, as MeCab segments it with the same dictionary. Build a Jieba dictionary directory from the mecab-jieba-0.1.3 archive. Users of Jieba: Expect Chinese text to be segmented as UD Chinese GSD segments it, finer than jieba (中华 / 人民 / 共和 / 国, 这 / 个), and as MeCab segments it with the same dictionary. Expect simple user dictionary words to cost −32768. Take the context IDs of detailed user dictionary rows from the left-id.def and right-id.def of mecab-jieba-0.1.3. Build a Jieba dictionary directory from the mecab-jieba-0.1.3 archive. Users of IPADIC or IPADIC-NEologd with text that contains ―, —, ～ or 〜: Expect entries spelled with ― or ～ to match text spelled the same way, as in MeCab, and text with — or 〜 to miss the 12 IPADIC and 1,085 IPADIC-NEologd entries that it found only through the old rewrite. With IPADIC, map — to ― and ～ to 〜 with the mapping character filter if both spellings should find the entries. Users who read token details such as the reading or the base form: Expect words with tied entries to get the details of the first CSV row, as in MeCab: with IPADIC, 狡い reads ズルイ, not コスイ. No setting restores the v6 output. In a user dictionary, expect the first of tied rows to be chosen. A user entry still wins a tie with a system entry, unlike in MeCab. Everyone who compares the segmentation with v6 or with MeCab: Expect the places where two segmentations cost exactly the same, few with the Japanese and Korean dictionaries and Jieba but about a quarter of the sentences with CC-CEDICT, to be segmented as MeCab segments them, with the last word that starts later (IPADIC 腸窒扶斯 is 腸 / 窒扶 / 斯, CC-CEDICT 電視台上班 is 電視 / 台上 / 班). No setting restores the v6 output. Language bindings and CLI: Remove normalize_details where you create Metadata: the Python keyword argument, the ninth positional argument of Ruby's Metadata.new, the last argument of PHP's Metadata constructor, and the normalizeDetails option in Node.js. Stop reading the property and the key of the same name in to_dict(), to_h, toArray() and toObject(). With lindera tokenize, expect the offsets of a line that starts with whitespace to index the input line, U+3000 at the start or end of a line to be a token (IPADIC, IPADIC-NEologd, UniDic), --keep-whitespace to output the spaces there, -N to give one result for an empty line or a line of spaces, and the wakati format to write an empty line for a line without tokens. To get the v6 offsets and tokens, remove the whitespace at the ends of each line first. With the WASM TokenizerBuilder, expect setKeepWhitespace() and the appended filters to apply to a dictionary set with setDictionaryInstance(), and a user dictionary set with setUserDictionaryInstance() to apply to a dictionary set with setDictionary(). With PHP, pass each argument its declared type: a value of the wrong type for an optional parameter, which v6 read as null, now throws an Exception. Cast strings such as $argv values with (int) or (float). With PHP, Node.js and WASM, pass integer arguments in the range of their setting: a value outside it, which v6 wrapped, now throws, as do a negative index and, in Node.js and WASM, a number that is not an integer. Pass a Mode to set_mode / setMode and to the Tokenizer constructor instead of "normal" or "decompose": Mode.normal() or Mode.decompose() (Ruby Lindera::Mode.normal, PHP Lindera\Mode::normal()), with a Penalty to customize decompose mode, or Mode.from_str(name) (Mode.fromStr in PHP, Node.js and WASM) for a name read at run time. Replace uses of the old Mode types, such as Python's Mode("normal"), Node.js's JsMode and WASM's Mode.Normal, in the same way. With Node.js and TypeScript, rename the type JsPenalty to Penalty. With the CLI, expect warnings on standard error, for example for a sentence cut after 32 KiB without a delimiter; set RUST_LOG=error to hide them. Nothing else to do beyond taking the 7.0.0 release, apart from the dictionary rebuild, the dictionary, whitespace, 、 and 。, N-best, unknown-word, default-category, dash and tilde, tied-entry and equal-cost items above, the lindera train and lindera build items, and the lindera tokenize, WASM, PHP, integer-argument, Mode, JsPenalty and CLI warning items.

839.body: Run the full test suite for a single crate: cargo test -p <crate> --all-features Note: CI does not use --all-features -- it runs each crate with a curated, crate-specific feature combination (see .github/workflows/regression.yml). The Makefile's per-crate pattern targets (make test-<crate>, make lint-<crate>) apply the same feature combinations CI uses and are the closest local equivalent. CI also tests lindera-segmenter and lindera once more with every dictionary embedded (on Linux only), which runs the tests gated on the other dictionaries; to do the same locally, run cargo test -p lindera --features embed-ipadic,embed-ipadic-neologd,embed-unidic,embed-sudachidict,embed-ko-dic,embed-cc-cedict,embed-jieba (and likewise for lindera-segmenter).

842.body: Verify code formatting matches the project style: cargo fmt --all -- --check To auto-fix formatting: cargo fmt --all Note: cargo fmt formats the Rust code only. For a language binding, make format-lindera-<binding> also formats the binding's Python, JavaScript, Ruby or PHP code, with the tools and versions make lint-lindera-<binding> checks it with (see below). make format-scripts does the same for the files outside the crates that make lint-scripts checks.

843.body: Run Clippy with warnings treated as errors: cargo clippy -- -D warnings Note: CI runs cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings for each crate, with the features it tests that crate with (see .github/workflows/test-crate.yml, and the language binding jobs in .github/workflows/regression.yml), so the test code is linted too. make lint-<crate> runs the same clippy command. Run clippy locally (e.g. via make lint) before opening a PR. For a language binding, make lint-lindera-<binding> then runs the binding's language-side linter, as the binding's CI job does: ruff for Python, Prettier for Node.js and WASM, RuboCop for Ruby, and PHP CS Fixer for PHP. Their versions are pinned (ruff and Prettier in the Makefile, RuboCop in lindera-ruby/Gemfile, PHP CS Fixer in composer.json), so a new release of a tool cannot fail CI on unchanged code. The targets install the pinned versions themselves, which needs the language's toolchain (Python 3, Node.js with npx, Bundler, Composer) and network access. make lint-scripts lints the hand-written files that belong to no binding, as the Lint scripts CI job does: the benchmark harness in scripts/benchmarks/, which the bindings share, and the JavaScript the docs load (docs/mermaid-init.js). It runs the same pinned tools, and checks each file with the rules of the binding written in its language, so it needs all four toolchains. make lint runs it after the crates.

845.body: Generate and open Rust API documentation: cargo doc --no-deps --open Check the crates' API documentation for rustdoc warnings, such as a broken intra-doc link or a public item linking to a private one: make check-docs Note: CI runs make check-docs and fails on any rustdoc warning. It documents every crate but the language bindings with all features: the libraries twice, once with public items only, as docs.rs publishes them, and once with private items too, whose doc comments only that second pass checks; then lindera-cli's binary, where the CLI's code lives, with its private items. It builds with dummy dictionaries (DOCS_RS=1) in its own target directory, target/check-docs, so it downloads no dictionary and leaves target/ alone. The language bindings are checked one at a time, since building each needs its language's toolchain: make check-docs-lindera-python # also -nodejs, -ruby, -php, -wasm Note: Each binding's CI job runs its target and fails on any rustdoc warning. The target documents the binding twice, public items only and then with private items too, with default features, which already enable every feature that adds or removes an item; no dictionary is built. lindera-ruby runs through the same RbConfig wrapper as make test-lindera-ruby, and lindera-wasm is documented for wasm32-unknown-unknown.
